docs.title: Existing Planetary Gearbox Replacement & Redesign
docs.text: If an existing planetary gearbox is discontinued, no longer fits the required ratio / output, or is wearing prematurely, overheating, developing backlash, making abnormal noise or damaging gears / bearings, the review should start from the actual assembly, interfaces and operating condition, not only from the old model number.

docs.title: “We Need to Keep the Motor and Mounting Interface, but Change the Gearbox. Can SigGear Review It?”
docs.text:
Yes. A replacement project can start from the existing gearbox, motor, drawing, STEP model, physical sample or measured interfaces.

The first review should separate two questions:

  1. What must remain unchanged? — motor, pilot, bolt pattern, shaft position, output interface, envelope or machine connection.
  2. What needs to change? — ratio, output speed, shaft / flange, torque capability, durability, backlash, bearing arrangement or production configuration.

SigGear can review the old unit against the real operating condition and determine whether the best path is a standard platform, a modified platform or a custom replacement.

Start Existing Gearbox Replacement Review Failure / Durability Analysis Keep Existing Motor — Review Interface

SigGear can review its 8–42 mm planetary gearbox platforms as starting points for a replacement or modified configuration. A replacement is not described as drop-in or fully compatible until the mechanical, performance and operating requirements have been checked.

Browse 8–42 mm Gearboxes Send Existing Unit / Drawing for Review

docs.title: What to Send First
docs.text:
The most useful starting information is:

  1. Existing gearbox model if known
  2. Old drawing, datasheet or measured dimensions
  3. Motor model and motor drawing
  4. Loaded motor speed and required output speed
  5. Continuous and peak torque / load
  6. Gear ratio if known
  7. Output shaft or flange geometry
  8. Motor-side shaft, pilot and mounting pattern
  9. Maximum allowed diameter and assembly length
  10. Duty cycle and operating environment

If an old physical sample is available, it can be useful for checking the interfaces and construction details that may not appear on a public drawing.

docs.title: If the Existing Gearbox Has Failed
docs.text:
Describe the observed failure rather than only requesting a stronger replacement.

Useful evidence can include:

  • worn or damaged gear stage
  • tooth wear or pitting
  • broken shaft or carrier
  • excessive backlash after use
  • bearing damage
  • overheating
  • abnormal noise
  • lubricant condition
  • load history
  • approximate operating hours / cycles
  • photos of the failed components

The failure evidence helps determine whether the review should focus on gear geometry, material / heat treatment, bearing arrangement, lubrication, stage selection, interface, duty cycle or another part of the system.

A replacement design should not assume that increasing one dimension or changing one material alone will solve the original failure.

docs.title: Common Replacement Scenarios
docs.text:
A replacement project does not always mean the original gearbox has failed.

Typical reasons include:

  • original supplier or model is no longer available
  • motor must remain unchanged
  • mounting pattern / pilot / shaft location must remain unchanged
  • output shaft or flange needs to change
  • output speed or ratio needs to change
  • the existing gearbox is too long or too large
  • gear or bearing durability needs improvement
  • backlash has increased beyond the application requirement
  • a prototype replacement is needed before repeat production
  • the customer wants one controlled replacement source for future production

The reason for replacement affects the engineering path.

docs.title: What Must Match — and What Can Change?
docs.text: Area Review question Motor interface Must the existing motor, shaft, pilot and hole pattern remain unchanged? Ratio Must the original ratio be retained, or can output speed change? Output interface Must the existing shaft / flange / key / mounting geometry remain unchanged? Envelope Which diameter, gearbox length and total assembly dimensions are fixed? Torque / load What are the real continuous and peak loads? External loads Are radial or axial loads applied to the output? Duty cycle Continuous running, intermittent operation, holding or repeated reversals? Precision Backlash, positioning or repeatability requirement? Production Prototype quantity, expected repeat volume and target schedule?

docs.title: Replacement Interface Checklist
docs.text:
Before a replacement is described as compatible, review the critical interfaces separately:

Interface Typical items to confirm Motor side motor shaft, pilot, mounting holes, pinion / input feature Gearbox envelope diameter, gearbox length, total assembly length Output side shaft / flange, key, bolt pattern, locating features Machine mounting bolt pattern, center position, locating geometry Motion ratio, output speed, direction Load continuous / peak torque, radial / axial load, duty cycle Precision backlash / repeatability requirement where applicable Production prototype quantity, repeat volume, inspection requirement

A dimensional match does not by itself establish torque, thermal, lifetime or operating compatibility.

docs.title: Start From the Closest SigGear Platform
docs.text:
The current public planetary range includes:

8P · 10P · 12P · 14P · 16P · 20P · 22P · 24P · 28P · 32P · 36P · 42P

Each frame has its own stage / ratio combinations, rated torque, length and interface. The nearest diameter is only a starting point.

docs.title: If the Motor Must Stay
docs.text:
When the customer motor cannot change, the motor-side interface becomes one of the primary design constraints.

The replacement review should check:

  • motor shaft diameter and usable length
  • input pinion or shaft feature
  • locating pilot
  • motor mounting-hole pattern
  • loaded operating speed
  • available motor + gearbox length
  • required output torque and speed

docs.title: If You Only Have an Old Unit or Physical Sample
docs.text:
A physical sample can help establish:

  • overall envelope
  • shaft / flange geometry
  • motor interface
  • mounting pattern
  • stage arrangement
  • visible wear or damage
  • dimensions missing from old documentation

The sample should be reviewed together with the actual operating condition. A worn component may no longer represent the original manufacturing dimension.

Drawing / STEP / Physical Sample Review

docs.title: From Replacement Prototype to Repeat Production
docs.text:
If the gearbox is part of an ongoing product, the replacement should be treated as a production program rather than only a one-off sample.

A typical path is:

Existing Unit / Interfaces → Replacement Engineering Review → Prototype → Application Validation → Design Refinement → Design Freeze → Pilot / Repeat Manufacturing

Prototype → Volume Production Manufacturing Equipment & Inspection

docs.title: “We Have a Robot Mechanism / STEP Model. Can SigGear Review a Custom Joint?”
docs.text:
Yes. A robot-joint project can start from the mechanism, STEP model, link geometry, torque-speed requirement, preferred motor / controller or an early prototype.

SigGear can review the transmission structure, motor, feedback, driver and mechanical interfaces as one actuator system. A public SG or CPM model can be used as a reference platform, but the project does not need to match a standard actuator exactly.

docs.title: Start From the Joint Requirement, Not From an Existing Actuator Model
docs.text:
A robotics project does not need to fit an existing SigGear actuator exactly.

You may already know the joint torque, speed and installation envelope. You may also have only a robot mechanism, link geometry, motor preference, STEP concept or early prototype.

SigGear develops and manufactures robot joint actuators, planetary actuator platforms and cycloidal joint modules for robotics and compact motion systems.

SigGear can review the joint as a system and evaluate the actuator gearbox or reducer, motor, sensing, driver and mechanical interfaces together.

Depending on the project, the engineering path may start from:

  • an existing SigGear planetary actuator
  • an existing SigGear cycloidal joint module
  • a gearbox-centered solution for the customer's own motor and controller
  • a motor + gearbox combination
  • a modified mechanical interface
  • a new compact actuator configuration based on the application requirements

Send Your Joint Requirement Humanoid and Bipedal Robot Joint Engineering Request Engineering Review

docs.title: What Can SigGear Supply?
docs.text:
Depending on the project and engineering feasibility, the supply scope may include:

  • gearbox / reducer only
  • motor + gearbox assembly
  • planetary robot joint actuator
  • cycloidal joint module
  • actuator with encoder
  • actuator with driver where applicable
  • modified mechanical interface
  • project-specific joint configuration

The exact configuration depends on torque, speed, packaging, motor, sensing, controller and mechanical-interface requirements.

docs.title: Project-Specific and OEM Development
docs.text: For OEM or project-specific robot joint programs, the engineering review can begin from an existing SigGear actuator platform, the customer's motor/controller architecture, or a new mechanical requirement. Final feasibility depends on the complete torque-speed requirement, packaging, interfaces, electronics configuration and production plan.

docs.title: What the Engineering Review Starts With
docs.text:
A meaningful robot-joint review normally needs the axis requirement rather than one isolated torque number.

Useful inputs include:

  • robot type and joint position
  • payload and moving-link mass
  • link length and center-of-gravity location
  • continuous torque
  • peak torque and peak duration
  • output speed and motion cycle
  • maximum diameter, thickness, length and weight
  • radial / axial load and overturning load where relevant
  • operating voltage and controller current limits
  • encoder and feedback requirement
  • driver and control mode
  • communication interface
  • power-off behavior and brake requirement
  • prototype quantity and expected production volume

If some of these are not known yet, send the mechanism, STEP model, sketch or the information already available. The engineering review can identify what needs to be calculated, measured or tested before the actuator architecture is fixed.

docs.title: Planetary, Cycloidal or Another Joint Architecture?
docs.text:
SigGear publishes both planetary robot joint actuators and cycloidal joint modules.

Neither structure should be selected from a general rule alone.

The choice needs to consider:

  • torque-speed requirement
  • installation diameter and axial thickness
  • motor speed and motor size
  • ratio
  • efficiency
  • backlash
  • external loads
  • thermal condition
  • noise target
  • backdrivability or holding requirement
  • encoder / driver architecture
  • prototype and production constraints

For a project where the transmission structure has not been decided, send the operating requirement first.

Planetary vs Cycloidal Selection Guide Integrated Joint vs Motor + Gearhead Custom Planetary Gearhead Engineering Custom Cycloidal Transmission Engineering

docs.title: Existing Planetary Joint Reference Platforms
docs.text:

docs.text:
SG-6010C currently has the most complete public Engineering Pack among the planetary joint actuators.

docs.text:
For cycloidal joint evaluation, CPM-80-25 has a public Engineering Pack including:

View CPM-80-25 View CPM-80-25 Measured Performance Data

docs.title: What Can Be Reviewed in a Custom Joint Project
docs.text:
Depending on the reference platform and project feasibility, the review may include:

Engineering area Examples Transmission planetary or cycloidal structure, ratio and gearbox architecture Motor motor type, speed, power, torque constant and mechanical interface where applicable Packaging outer diameter, axial thickness, housing and total joint envelope Output flange, shaft, locating feature and robot-side mounting interface Feedback Hall / encoder arrangement supported by the selected configuration Driver integrated or external driver architecture Control position, velocity or torque control where supported by the selected driver Communication CAN, RS485 or other supported project-specific interface Safety brake, power-off behavior and mechanical stops where required Mechanical load radial, axial and overturning load review Integration cables, connectors, housing and assembly arrangement

Not every item can be changed independently. A change to motor, ratio, size, driver or interface may affect torque, speed, thermal behavior, weight, efficiency, life, control limits and cost.

docs.title: If You Do Not Know the Required Joint Torque
docs.text:
A robot team can still start the discussion before the torque value is finalized.

Useful inputs include:

  • supported mass
  • link mass
  • payload
  • link length
  • center-of-gravity location
  • acceleration target
  • external force
  • joint angle range
  • motion cycle
  • whether the axis works against gravity

For a first single-axis screening, gravity, acceleration and external-force torque can be estimated before the actuator is shortlisted.

Open the Robot Joint Actuator Selection Guide

docs.title: If You Have a Motor or Controller Already
docs.text:
Some robotics teams already have a preferred motor, driver or control stack.

In that case, send the available:

  • motor drawing and shaft details
  • motor speed / voltage / power data
  • controller current limits
  • encoder requirement
  • communication requirement
  • available installation space
  • required output torque and speed

SigGear can then evaluate whether the project should use a gearbox-centered joint solution, a motor + gearbox assembly or another integrated actuator approach.

Motor + Gearbox Integration Engineering Prototype → Design-In → Production Open the Engineering Center

docs.title: Robot and AI Hardware Applications
docs.text:
Custom joint and compact actuator development may be relevant for:

  • humanoid robots
  • quadruped robots
  • robotic arms
  • exoskeletons
  • rehabilitation robots
  • service robots
  • compact rotary automation axes
  • AI-enabled hardware products that require compact controlled motion

For smaller mechanisms such as dexterous hands, grippers and compact end effectors, a micro planetary gearbox or gear-motor architecture may be more appropriate than the larger published joint modules.

Browse Micro Gear Motors Robot Gripper and Dexterous-Hand Applications

These are application areas where SigGear transmission products and engineering review may be relevant. They are not claims that SigGear has a public production case in every listed application.

docs.title: Engineering Development Path
docs.text:
A custom robot-joint project may move through:

Joint Requirement / Robot CAD / Existing Prototype → Torque and Motion Review → Transmission Architecture Review → Motor / Encoder / Driver Review → Mechanical Interface and Packaging Review → Configuration Drawing → Prototype / Sample → Representative Joint Test → Parameter / Interface Refinement → Design Confirmation → Pilot Preparation → Production

The exact path depends on how much of the robot architecture is already fixed.

docs.title: What to Send First
docs.text:
You do not need to prepare a complete joint specification before contacting SigGear.

For a first review, send what you already have:

  1. robot type and joint position
  2. link / load information
  3. target torque if known
  4. target speed
  5. maximum joint diameter and thickness
  6. operating voltage
  7. motor / controller preference if already selected
  8. encoder / communication requirement if already defined
  9. drawing, CAD screenshot or mechanism sketch
  10. prototype quantity and expected production volume if known

If several values are still unknown, the project can start from the robot mechanism and design intent.

docs.title: Confidential Robotics Projects
docs.text:
Robot and AI-hardware development often involves unreleased mechanisms, customer CAD and project-specific actuator architecture.

Those projects may be covered by confidentiality agreements and cannot be shown publicly.

SigGear therefore uses public actuator platforms, gearbox platforms, CAD resources, mechanical interfaces and test data to demonstrate real engineering capability without exposing confidential customer designs.

docs.title: Custom Gearbox & Transmission Review — Start From Your Motor, Drawing or Failed Unit
docs.text:
Many precision transmission projects do not start with a catalog model.

They start with a practical engineering problem:

“Here is my motor.”

“Here is our drawing.”

“Our existing gearbox needs replacement / redesign.”

“We need 20 prototypes first, then thousands in production.”

These are exactly the kinds of projects SigGear is built to review.

SigGear is a precision transmission manufacturer focused on custom engineering, prototype development, repeatable volume manufacturing and production delivery. The public 8–42 mm planetary gearboxes, cycloidal reducers and robot joint actuators are reference platforms; many customer-specific products and production programs remain confidential.

Start an Engineering Review Custom Manufacturing & Volume Production

docs.title: “Here Is My Motor.”
docs.text:
If the motor is already selected, the transmission needs to be reviewed around the real motor interface and operating point.

Useful information includes:

  • motor model or drawing
  • loaded operating speed
  • shaft diameter and usable length
  • locating pilot
  • mounting-hole pattern
  • target output speed
  • continuous and peak load
  • maximum transmission diameter and available assembly length

The final reduction ratio does not need to be known before the first review.

Planetary Gearbox for an Existing Motor Start Existing-Motor Review

docs.title: “Here Is Our Drawing / STEP / Sample.”
docs.text:
A project can also start from a customer STEP model, mechanism drawing, installation envelope, marked-up sketch or physical sample.

SigGear can review:

  • available diameter and axial length
  • motor-side interface
  • output shaft / flange
  • locating features
  • ratio and speed requirement
  • bearing / external-load arrangement
  • encoder, driver and communication requirements where applicable
  • manufacturability of the proposed transmission arrangement

A simple mechanism drawing, STEP model or physical sample can be enough to begin identifying the missing engineering inputs.

Custom Gearbox From Drawing / STEP Start Drawing / STEP Review

docs.title: “Our Existing Gearbox Needs Replacement / Redesign.”
docs.text:
If an existing transmission must be replaced because it is failing, discontinued or no longer fits the required ratio / output / interface, the review should start from the actual unit, interfaces and operating condition.

Useful inputs include:

  • old gearbox model / drawing
  • actual motor
  • operating speed
  • continuous and peak load
  • duty cycle
  • photos of failed components
  • approximate service hours / cycles
  • output shaft and mounting interface
  • available installation space
  • physical sample if available

The objective is not to promise a “perfect replacement” from a photo. It is to identify what must remain unchanged, what needs to change, and why the original unit no longer meets the project requirement before evaluating a revised transmission.

Replacement Planetary Gearbox Review Start Replacement / Redesign Review

docs.title: “We Need Prototypes First, Then Thousands in Production.”
docs.text:
A custom project should be evaluated as a manufacturing program, not only as a sample request.

A typical path can be:

Requirement / Existing Design → Feasibility Review → Prototype / Sample → Application Test → Design Refinement → Design Freeze → Pilot Preparation → Repeatable Volume Manufacturing

For production-oriented projects, useful commercial / manufacturing information includes:

  • prototype quantity
  • expected annual volume or forecast
  • target pilot timing
  • target production timing
  • critical inspection requirements
  • packaging / labeling requirements where relevant
  • expected batch / delivery plan

SigGear works to support short production lead times for applicable volume programs after the configuration, quantity and production plan are confirmed. Actual lead time remains project-specific.

Prototype → Volume Production Start Prototype-to-Volume Review

docs.title: Confidential / NDA Projects
docs.text:
Many custom precision-transmission programs involve unreleased customer products, proprietary mechanisms and future production plans.

SigGear does not publish confidential customer designs as marketing case studies.

If an NDA is required before detailed drawings are shared, the first discussion can stay at the level of:

  • application category
  • target motion
  • envelope
  • torque / speed
  • production volume
  • confidentiality requirement

Detailed STEP models, drawings and project files can be exchanged after the appropriate confidentiality process is agreed.

docs.text:
Depending on engineering feasibility:

  • reduction ratio
  • input pinion / shaft

Not every parameter can be changed independently, and a change to ratio, motor, size or load can affect other parts of the design.

docs.text:
SigGear's public engineering resources are designed to support both standard-product evaluation and custom transmission development. The released products are public reference platforms; many customer-specific products and production programs remain confidential.

This Engineering Center is organized around the way an engineer normally evaluates a transmission product:

find a relevant model -> check the published data -> evaluate the mechanical interface -> test a sample -> freeze the configuration for design-in.

Use the public resources below for preliminary engineering evaluation. Robot actuator and planetary gearbox engineering documents include public datasheets, STEP models, mechanical-interface references and measured test data where released. Configuration-specific production drawings, driver/firmware documentation and other controlled files are supplied according to the selected product and project stage.

docs.title: Design-In Checklist
docs.text:
Use this checklist when a SigGear product has passed preliminary evaluation and is being considered for the customer's prototype, BOM or design freeze.

The purpose is to prevent a sample configuration from being copied into a final design without confirming the exact mechanical, electrical and operating conditions.

docs.title: Planetary Design-In Review Decision
docs.text:
If you arrived from the Sample Validation Workflow with a validated 8P–42P planetary candidate, this panel rechecks the model + stage + published ratio and interprets only the normalized sample-validation status / outcome.

Checking the candidate and sample-review context...

Automated preliminary decision

This automated status is only a workflow routing aid. It does not approve Design-In, freeze the design, approve pilot production or release the product for mass production.

Input Normalized value Meaning Candidate Revalidated against current published ratio-stage data. Sample validation status Standardized customer-side sample workflow result. Engineering outcome Standardized next-direction selected in the sample workflow. Manual Engineering Milestones Design Frozen — Human confirmation required

Do not treat the design as frozen until the exact configuration, controlled drawing revision, validated operating point, applicable motor / driver / firmware configuration and remaining risks have been reviewed and confirmed by the responsible engineering / project teams.

Pilot Preparation Ready — Human confirmation required

Do not treat the project as pilot-ready until Design Freeze has been confirmed and the pilot quantity, schedule, inspection requirements, change-control expectations and project-specific documentation needs have been agreed.

Prepare Design-In Review Email Open Datasheet Open Mechanical Interface Open Pilot Preparation Checklist Prototype → Pilot → Production

The Design-In decision panel does not receive the customer's free-text test notes, measured torque / speed / temperature values or other private validation details through the URL.

docs.title: 1. Product Identity
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • exact model
  • reduction ratio / stage count
  • driver or no-driver configuration
  • encoder / sensor configuration where applicable
  • motor configuration for gearbox-only or matched motor + gearbox assemblies
  • cable / connector configuration where applicable

docs.title: 2. Mechanical Interface
docs.text:
Confirm against the applicable controlled information:

  • overall envelope
  • mounting-hole pattern
  • locating diameter / pilot
  • output shaft or output flange
  • key / spline / pinion definition where applicable
  • motor-side interface
  • cable / connector clearance
  • required assembly direction
  • radial and axial load direction

A public simplified STEP is intended for early packaging and mounting evaluation. Use the controlled configuration drawing for final tooling or production release.

docs.title: 3. Operating Point
docs.text:
Confirm the actual application requirement:

  • continuous torque
  • momentary / peak torque
  • peak duration
  • output speed
  • acceleration and deceleration
  • motion cycle
  • duty cycle
  • ambient temperature
  • cooling condition
  • external radial / axial loads
  • backlash or positioning requirement where relevant

Do not base final selection only on a single peak-torque or no-load-speed value.

docs.title: 4. Electrical and Control Configuration
docs.text:
For motorized or driver-equipped products, confirm:

  • operating voltage
  • current limits
  • driver version
  • encoder configuration
  • communication interface
  • control mode
  • firmware / protocol revision where relevant
  • power-off behavior
  • brake requirement if applicable

Detailed control documentation should match the ordered driver and firmware configuration.

docs.title: 5. Sample Test Outcome
docs.text:
Record what the sample actually demonstrated.

Useful evidence includes:

  • mechanical fit confirmed
  • first power-up / communication confirmed
  • no-load motion confirmed
  • representative load test completed
  • temperature behavior reviewed where relevant
  • observed noise / vibration reviewed where relevant
  • faults or integration issues resolved
  • remaining risks or assumptions documented

A Sample Validation Workflow status of Ready to Submit for Design-In Review means the recorded sample steps are complete enough to submit for engineering review. It does not mean the configuration is already Design-In approved, frozen or production released.

docs.title: 6. Configuration Freeze
docs.text:
Before releasing the next prototype or pilot build, confirm:

  • exact product configuration
  • controlled drawing revision
  • agreed customized features, if any
  • motor / gearbox / driver combination
  • cable and connector definition
  • software / protocol version where applicable
  • prototype or pilot quantity

If a later hardware or firmware revision is introduced, re-check the affected interface rather than assuming it is identical to the sample.

docs.title: 7. Production and Change-Control Inputs
docs.text:
For a project moving beyond prototype, discuss:

  • expected pilot quantity
  • expected annual volume
  • target schedule
  • critical inspection requirements
  • labeling / packaging requirements if relevant
  • change-notification expectations
  • any project-specific quality documentation

Availability and scope depend on the selected product and project requirements.

docs.title: Design-In Review Decision States
docs.text:
Status Meaning How it is set Continue Evaluation Sample evidence or the next-direction decision is not complete enough for formal Design-In review. Website may route automatically from the normalized sample workflow. Engineering Revision Required A sample issue or requested configuration change must be reviewed before Design-In. Website may route automatically from the normalized sample workflow. Design-In Review Ready The validated candidate and sample workflow are ready to be submitted for formal engineering Design-In review. Website may route automatically, but this is not Design-In approval. Design Frozen Exact configuration and controlled revision have been reviewed and formally confirmed for the project. Human confirmation required. Pilot Preparation Ready Design Freeze is confirmed and pilot quantity, schedule, inspection and change-control inputs are agreed. Human confirmation required.

The website never automatically promotes a project to Design Frozen, Pilot Preparation Ready or Production Released.

docs.title: Design-In Gate
docs.text:
Before treating a product as design-in ready, the project should be able to answer:

  1. Which exact SigGear configuration is being designed in?
  2. Which controlled drawing or interface definition is being used?
  3. Which operating condition was validated by the sample?
  4. Which driver / firmware / communication configuration applies?
  5. What still needs confirmation before the next build?

If any of these remain unclear, keep the project in engineering evaluation rather than freezing the design.

docs.title: Sample Validation Workflow
docs.text:
The goal of a sample evaluation is not only to confirm that a product can rotate or transmit torque. It should also answer whether the selected configuration is suitable for the customer's mechanical, electrical and operating conditions.

This workflow is intended to make the first evaluation more structured and reduce avoidable setup delays.

docs.title: Planetary Candidate Sample Validation
docs.text:
If you arrived from a validated 8P–42P Candidate Design-In Pack, this panel rechecks the model + stage + published ratio before creating a sample-validation record.

Checking the planetary candidate against current published data...

This is a customer-side evaluation aid. A recorded “Pass” means the evaluator marked that step as acceptable in their test; it is not an independent SigGear certification or production approval.

1. Configuration received Not checked Pass — sample matches expected configuration Issue — configuration mismatch or uncertainty 2. Mechanical fit Not checked Pass — fit / mounting acceptable for this test Issue — fit / mounting needs review 3. No-load / free-rotation check Not checked Pass — basic no-load / free-rotation check acceptable Issue — alignment, drag, motion or setup concern 4. Functional test Not checked Pass — required basic function demonstrated Issue — output / motion / behavior needs review 5. Representative application-load test Not checked Pass — representative mechanism / load test acceptable Issue — representative application test needs review Engineering outcome Not decided yet Keep current configuration for next review Review a different ratio / stage Review motor / input-side configuration Revise mounting / shaft / interface More testing required Submit current configuration for Design-In review Test operating condition / evidence Issue / observation notes Validation status

Validation in Progress — record each step before submitting the configuration for Design-In review.

Copy Validation Summary Prepare Validation Email to SigGear Open Datasheet Open Mechanical Interface Open Design-In Review

The detailed operating condition and free-text observations stay in your browser until you copy the summary or open your email client. They are not sent to GA4.

docs.title: Before the Sample Is Ordered
docs.text:
Confirm the exact configuration being evaluated.

At minimum, record:

  • product model
  • ratio or output-speed target
  • driver / no-driver configuration where applicable
  • encoder requirement where applicable
  • operating voltage where applicable
  • required communication interface where applicable
  • mounting or shaft requirements that affect the sample
  • sample quantity

Use the public Engineering Pack before ordering when one is available.

Open the Engineering Center

docs.title: When the Sample Is Received
docs.text:
Before installation:

  1. confirm the model and quantity received
  2. compare the physical configuration with the order or quotation
  3. check for visible shipping damage
  4. identify the exact driver / connector / cable configuration where applicable
  5. use the documentation matched to that configuration

If anything is unclear, confirm the configuration before wiring or modifying the sample.

docs.title: Step 1 - Mechanical Fit
docs.text:
Check the sample against the customer's assembly:

  • outer diameter and axial length
  • mounting-hole pattern
  • output shaft or output flange
  • locating features
  • cable and connector clearance
  • motor-side interface for gearbox-only evaluations
  • direction of external radial and axial loads

For public models, use the released simplified STEP for packaging and mounting evaluation. Use the controlled drawing before final production release.

docs.title: Step 2 - First Power-Up or No-Load Check
docs.text:
For actuator or motorized configurations, first confirm the basic setup before applying the real application load.

Typical checks include:

  • supply voltage
  • wiring and connector orientation
  • communication link where applicable
  • enable / basic command response
  • direction of motion
  • encoder feedback where applicable
  • no-load motion

Detailed wiring, protocol and firmware-specific instructions must match the actual driver configuration.

For a gearbox-only sample, first confirm free assembly, input/output alignment and the selected motor interface before loaded testing.

docs.title: Step 3 - Functional Test
docs.text:
Run the motion required by the application and record the operating condition.

Useful information includes:

  • output speed
  • applied or estimated load
  • motion cycle
  • acceleration / deceleration behavior
  • current where applicable
  • temperature where relevant
  • observed backlash, vibration or noise where relevant
  • any communication or control fault

Do not compare a short sample test directly with a lifetime or continuous-duty claim unless the applicable rating and test condition are documented for that configuration.

docs.title: Step 4 - Application Test
docs.text:
After the basic function is stable, evaluate the sample in the real or representative mechanism.

Confirm:

  • actual installation geometry
  • actual load direction
  • continuous and peak load condition
  • peak duration
  • duty cycle
  • ambient / cooling condition
  • power-off behavior if important
  • controller / current-limit conditions for motorized actuators

docs.title: If a Problem Appears
docs.text:
Send the smallest useful set of evidence first:

  • exact model and configuration
  • supply voltage
  • controller / driver information
  • command or operating mode
  • what was expected
  • what actually happened
  • fault code or log if available
  • short video or photo if it helps show the issue

This is usually more useful than sending a long general description without the operating condition.

docs.text:
A successful sample test should lead to a concrete engineering decision, for example:

  • keep the current configuration
  • change the ratio
  • change the motor / driver
  • revise the mounting or output interface
  • request a controlled drawing
  • integrate into the next prototype
  • prepare for Design-In

docs.title: SigGear Testing, Metrology & Validation Evidence
docs.text:
This page separates three different things that are often mixed together in gearbox marketing:

  1. test and inspection capability
  2. real measured test records
  3. published product specifications

They are not interchangeable. A photograph of test equipment does not create a product specification, and a measured result from one model must not be transferred to another model.

Selected real equipment images from SigGear company material. They show dimensional metrology, gear inspection / measurement, environmental test equipment and a transmission test fixture. The image demonstrates physical testing and inspection capability; it is not a model-specific test report.

docs.title: Documented Testing and Inspection Scope
docs.text:
SigGear company equipment material documents testing and inspection resources including:

  • coordinate measuring equipment
  • gear inspection equipment
  • gear meshing inspection
  • optical / two-dimensional measurement
  • brushless-motor comprehensive testing
  • dynamometer and eddy-current dynamometer testing
  • concentricity measurement
  • backlash inspection
  • high-low temperature testing
  • thermal-shock testing
  • quiet-room acoustic testing
  • salt-spray testing
  • microscopy and other dimensional inspection

The applicable equipment, fixture, test method and acceptance criteria depend on the product and project requirement.

docs.title: Released Public Test Records
docs.text: Only source-backed results that have been reviewed for public use are treated as public test evidence.

docs.title: CPM-80-25 Measured Dynamometer Data
docs.text:
The current public CPM-80-25 performance page contains representative measured dynamometer points at 24 V, 36 V and 48 V.

These are measured observations under the documented test setup. They are not generic SigGear gearbox performance values and must not be transferred to the miniature planetary series.

View CPM-80-25 Measured Performance Data

docs.title: SG-6010HB Thermal Test Record
docs.text:
The current public SG-6010HB thermal record publishes source-backed temperature-rise timing under documented stall and 110 rpm load conditions.

The page intentionally leaves undefined source fields uninterpreted instead of converting them into unsupported specifications.

View SG-6010HB Thermal Test Record

docs.title: 8P-42P Planetary Gearbox Evidence Boundary
docs.text:
The 8P-42P planetary gearbox series already has public model pages, Datasheets, Mechanical Interface references, simplified STEP CAD and real product photographs.

However, this website does not currently publish one universal torque-efficiency curve, noise curve, lifetime result or backlash test report that applies across all 12 planetary frame sizes.

Do not transfer:

  • CPM-80-25 dynamometer data
  • SG-6010HB thermal data
  • another planetary frame size's measured result
  • a single sample result from one ratio or stage count

to a different 8P-42P configuration.

For a planetary gearbox test result to become public engineering evidence, the test record should identify the exact configuration and conditions.

docs.title: Minimum Record for a Planetary Gearbox Test
docs.text:
A useful public test record should normally include:

  • exact gearbox model / frame size
  • reduction ratio
  • stage count
  • motor model or input source
  • supply voltage and current limit where applicable
  • input speed
  • measured output speed
  • applied output torque or load
  • temperature / ambient condition where relevant
  • test equipment or measurement method
  • sample or configuration identification
  • test date or source revision
  • clear distinction between measured points and rated specifications

For torque-efficiency testing, input power, output torque, output speed and the efficiency calculation basis should all be traceable to the same test setup.

docs.title: How Test Evidence Is Used
docs.text:
Test evidence supports engineering evaluation, but final Design-In should still match the customer's:

  • motor
  • ratio and stage count
  • duty cycle
  • continuous and peak load
  • mounting condition
  • ambient and cooling condition
  • life / cycle target
  • noise or backlash acceptance criteria

A source-backed test can support a decision. It should not be expanded into a broader claim than the test actually proves.

docs.title: 32P Planetary Gearbox - Public STEP Design-In Pack
docs.text:
This page brings together the current public engineering resources for the SigGear 32P 32 mm planetary gearbox so an engineer can move from preliminary selection to early mechanical design-in without searching across separate pages.

The current downloadable STEP is a simplified 4-stage reference. It is intended for packaging, mounting and early integration work. It is not the controlled production model and must not be used as a universal 1-4 stage production STEP file.

docs.title: Design-In Path
docs.text:
1. Select the frame and operating range using the Technical Datasheet.
  2. Check mounting and shaft interfaces using the Mechanical Interface.
  3. Place the public simplified STEP into the early assembly or packaging model.
  4. Check the motor-side interface and operating point using the Motor Integration Guide.
  5. Validate the selected configuration with a sample under the real application load and duty cycle.
  6. Request configuration-specific controlled CAD / drawing before final tooling, design freeze or production release.

docs.title: Current Public Reference Configuration
docs.text:
Item Public reference Model 32P Nominal outer diameter 32 mm Public CAD stage 4-stage reference 4-stage gearbox body length 52.95 mm Nominal output shaft diameter 8 mm Output shaft extension 21.6 mm (+0.1 / -0.3 mm) Reduction ratio range of 32P family 3.5:1-509.1:1 Rated allowable torque range of 32P family 35.0-80.0 kgf.cm Maximum momentary torque range of 32P family 70.0-160.0 kgf.cm Backlash at no load <= 1.2 deg Continuous permissible input speed Motor/configuration dependent; confirm selected operating point

Maximum momentary torque is not a continuous operating rating. The torque and ratio ranges above cover the published 1-4 stage 32P family; the public STEP itself represents only the 4-stage external envelope.

docs.title: 4. Motor Integration Guide
docs.text:
Use this guide when the project starts from an existing motor or requires a matched motor + gearbox assembly.

Open 32P Motor Integration Guide

docs.title: What the Public STEP Is For
docs.text:
The simplified public CAD can be used for:

  • installation-envelope review
  • early assembly layout
  • mounting-position review
  • output-shaft packaging
  • motor-side packaging review
  • preliminary interference checking
  • early prototype mechanical design

It intentionally does not expose the internal planetary gear train, carrier details, bearings, internal fasteners or manufacturing-only internal geometry.

docs.title: What Still Requires Controlled Engineering Data
docs.text:
Before final tooling, design freeze or production release, confirm the exact configuration against controlled information.

Required confirmation includes:

  • selected reduction ratio
  • stage count
  • controlled drawing revision
  • motor shaft and locating interface
  • output key / keyseat definition
  • final mounting tolerances
  • radial and axial load direction
  • continuous and momentary torque
  • output speed
  • duty cycle
  • ambient and thermal condition
  • prototype and expected annual quantity

For 1-, 2- or 3-stage CAD, request the configuration-matched file rather than modifying the public 4-stage model.

docs.title: Sample Validation Before Design Freeze
docs.text:

docs.title: 42P Planetary Gearbox - Design-In Pack
docs.text:
This page brings together the current engineering resources for the SigGear 42P 42 mm planetary gearbox so an engineer can move from preliminary frame selection to interface review, configuration-specific STEP / drawing review and sample validation.

The 42P currently has a public Datasheet, a public Mechanical Interface based on controlled drawing SG01PD42, and a simplified public 4-stage STEP for early mechanical packaging and Design-In.

For early design-in, use the published envelope and interface references below. For final CAD placement, tooling or design freeze, request the configuration-matched controlled CAD.

docs.title: Design-In Path
docs.text:
1. Check frame size, ratio range and torque range in the Technical Datasheet.
  2. Review the output and motor-side interfaces in the Mechanical Interface.
  3. Select the likely stage count and body length from the published configuration table.
  4. Send the selected ratio / stage and motor interface to request configuration-matched CAD.
  5. Validate the selected gearbox with a sample under the real load, speed and duty cycle.
  6. Freeze the configuration only after the controlled drawing / CAD revision is confirmed.

docs.text:

Maximum momentary torque is not a continuous operating rating.

docs.title: Planetary Gearbox Candidate Design-In Pack
docs.text:
Use this page after the SigGear Ratio & Stage Selection Tool has narrowed the project to a published model + stage + ratio candidate.

This page does not convert the public 4-stage STEP into stage-specific production CAD. It rechecks the candidate against the current published ratio-stage data and explains which resources can be used for preliminary Design-In.

Checking the candidate against current published data...

Validated Published Candidate Model Diameter Stage Published ratio Gearbox body length Rated allowable torque Maximum momentary torque Efficiency CAD Status for This Candidate Open Datasheet Open Mechanical Interface Open Public 4-Stage STEP Request Controlled CAD / Engineering Review Plan / Record Sample Validation Open Dedicated Model Design-In Pack What Each Resource Is For Resource Use it for Do not assume Datasheet Published stage count, ratio, gearbox body length, torque and efficiency references. That the candidate is suitable without checking motor operating point, duty cycle and external loads. Mechanical Interface Public mounting, shaft and stage-dependent envelope references from the controlled drawing. That every final tolerance or customer-specific motor adapter is already released. Public STEP Frame-level external-interface review using the released simplified 4-stage reference. That it represents a 1-, 2- or 3-stage candidate, or that it is final production CAD. Controlled configuration CAD / drawing Exact selected stage / ratio / interface review before design freeze, tooling or production release. Availability before SigGear confirms the project configuration. Controlled CAD Review Readiness Before treating a configuration-specific CAD request as ready for engineering review, the Project Brief checks five items: 1. **Candidate configuration** — validated model + stage + published ratio. 2. **Motor / drive-side interface** — existing motor drawing / model, shaft and mounting reference, or a drive-side configuration confirmed by SigGear. 3. **Output interface** — required shaft, keyway, flange or mounting arrangement. 4. **Load / duty** — continuous / peak load information and duty cycle / peak duration. 5. **Installation envelope** — maximum diameter and/or length constraint. Use the **Request Controlled CAD / Engineering Review** button above to carry the validated candidate into the Project Brief and check these five gates. **Ready for CAD Review** means enough information is present for SigGear engineering to begin a configuration-specific review. It does **not** mean controlled CAD has already been approved or released. Before Design Freeze Confirm at minimum: - selected model, stage and ratio - exact gearbox body length - motor operating speed and duty cycle - continuous and peak load - radial / axial shaft loads where relevant - motor shaft, pilot and mounting interface - output interface - controlled CAD / drawing revision - sample validation in the actual application

The candidate shown here remains a preliminary Design-In candidate until SigGear engineering confirms the exact configuration.

docs.title: SG-6010C Technical Datasheet v1.0
docs.text:
Status: Approved for Public Release date: 2026-09-28

SG-6010C is a compact integrated planetary robot joint actuator for applications that require a thin axial profile, moderate torque and relatively high output speed.

Driver, encoder, communication and closed-loop functions apply only to the configuration confirmed in the quotation.

docs.title: Key Performance
docs.text:
Parameter Value Outer diameter 80.0 mm Product thickness 34.07 mm Reduction ratio 9.67:1 Backlash 15-20 arcmin Rated output torque 6 Nm Peak output torque 18 Nm Rated output speed 310 rpm No-load output speed 400 rpm Weight 377 +/- 10 g Allowable radial force 250 N Allowable axial force 100 N

Note

Peak torque is not a continuous rating. Peak-torque duration, duty cycle and thermal suitability must be confirmed for the actual application.

docs.title: Motor and Electrical Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Motor power 328 W Operating voltage 24-48 VDC Phase damping 224 uOhm Phase inductance 235 uH Phase current full scale 33 A Rated bus current 12 A Static working bus current 0.08 A Motor torque constant 0.0606 Nm/A Motor structure 18 slots / 20 poles Thermistor 10 kOhm B3435 +/-1% NTC B value 3435 Back EMF constant 0.0727 Vs/rad Motor KV value 104 rpm/V

docs.title: Encoder, Driver and Control
docs.text:
The driver-equipped configuration can use the MA600 16-bit single-turn absolute magnetic encoder.

Available control functions for the confirmed driver-equipped configuration can include:

  • Position control
  • Velocity control
  • Torque control
  • MIT-style motion control
  • PID parameter adjustment
  • Calibration and user-zero configuration

docs.title: Communication and Expansion
docs.text:
Publicly documented interfaces for the driver-equipped configuration include:

  • CAN
  • USB Type-C for configuration and debugging
  • Second encoder interface supporting I2C / UART on applicable driver-equipped configurations
  • Expansion interfaces subject to the selected driver configuration

RS485 and EtherCAT can be evaluated through project-specific expansion hardware.

Driver hardware and firmware can evolve by ordered configuration. Confirm the driver and firmware configuration for the quoted unit before integration.

docs.text:
Status: Public engineering evaluation reference Release date: 2026-10-06

SG-6010D is an 80 mm integrated planetary robot joint actuator for projects that require a higher torque level than the SG-6010C reference platform.

This public datasheet consolidates the specifications already published on the current SG-6010D product page. Driver, encoder, communication and closed-loop functions depend on the ordered configuration and must be confirmed in the quotation.

docs.title: Key Performance
docs.text:
Parameter Published value Transmission structure Planetary gearbox Outer diameter 80.0 mm Product thickness 58.77 mm Reduction ratio 28.13:1 Backlash 15-30 arcmin Operating voltage 24-48 VDC Motor power 328 W Rated output speed 100 rpm No-load output speed 170 rpm Rated output torque 16 Nm Peak output torque 50 Nm Weight 791 g Allowable radial force 1000 N Allowable axial force 400 N

Warning

Peak torque is not a continuous rating. Peak-torque duration, current limit, duty cycle and thermal suitability must be confirmed for the actual application.

docs.title: Configuration Boundary
docs.text:
SG-6010D can be supplied in configurations that include:

  • Motor + planetary gearbox
  • Motor + planetary gearbox + integrated driver + encoder

The final driver, encoder, connector, cable and firmware configuration is confirmed by quotation and order documentation.

docs.title: Driver-Equipped Configuration
docs.text:
SigGear has confirmed that the SG6010 driver platform documented in the current SG6010 user manual applies to the driver-equipped SG-6010D configuration.

  • Velocity control

  • CANopen (CiA301 / CiA302 / CiA402)

EtherCAT and other expansion interfaces remain project-specific and require confirmation.

docs.text:
Status: Public engineering integration reference Release date: 2026-10-06

SigGear has confirmed that the current SG6010 driver platform documented in the SG6010 user manual applies to the driver-equipped SG-6010D configuration.

This page summarizes the integration information that is suitable for public engineering evaluation. Firmware revision and ordered hardware configuration must still be confirmed before final integration.

docs.title: Driver Electrical Reference
docs.text:
Parameter Confirmed manual value Rated driver voltage 15~48 V DC Minimum / maximum driver voltage 12/72 V DC Rated current 6 A Maximum line current 30 A Maximum phase current 90 A Standby power consumption <10 mA CAN maximum bitrate 1 Mbps USB Type-C rate 10 Mbps Encoder resolution 16-bit single-turn absolute Driver operating temperature -20°C to 70°C Motor over-temperature alarm 90°C, adjustable Driver over-temperature alarm 90°C, adjustable

Warning

These are driver-platform limits and are not a substitute for the SG-6010D actuator operating limits, current limits, torque limits or thermal validation for a specific application.

docs.title: Confirmed Interfaces
docs.text:
The driver platform includes or supports:

  • Power + CAN integrated connector
  • USB Type-C debugging / host communication
  • Second encoder interface using I2C or UART
  • SWD programming / debugging
  • Motor temperature input
  • Brake / braking-resistor interface
  • Minimum / maximum limit-switch inputs
  • Expansion interface for additional functions

The expansion slot can support additional interfaces such as RS485 and other project-specific expansion hardware. EtherCAT remains subject to project configuration and confirmation.

docs.title: CAN Simple
docs.text:
The SG6010 driver manual documents the CAN Simple protocol with:

  • Standard 11-bit CAN ID
  • 8-byte data frame
  • Configurable node ID
  • Configurable CAN bitrate
  • Factory default CAN bitrate documented as 500 kbps
  • Maximum CAN bitrate documented as 1 Mbps

docs.title: CANopen
docs.text:
The same driver platform supports CANopen and the manual documents implementation against:

  • CiA301
  • CiA302
  • CiA402

An EDS file is used for CANopen integration. Firmware / EDS revision must be matched to the delivered driver.

docs.title: RS485 / Modbus RTU
docs.text:
RS485 with Modbus RTU is supported on the confirmed SG6010 driver platform when the corresponding RS485 interface / expansion configuration is supplied.

The manual documents up to 115200 bps for the RS485 implementation.

docs.title: Confirmed Control Modes
docs.text:
The driver platform supports:

  • Position control
  • Velocity control
  • Torque control
  • MIT-style motion control

The manual further documents filtered / trajectory / circular position modes, direct / ramped velocity control and direct / ramped torque control.

docs.title: Encoder and Feedback
docs.text:
The driver platform uses a 16-bit single-turn absolute magnetic encoder in the driver-equipped configuration.

The second-encoder interface can communicate through:

  • I2C
  • UART

Final second-encoder hardware, mounting and firmware configuration must be confirmed for the order.

docs.title: Integration Boundary
docs.text:
Before final integration, confirm:

  • Driver hardware revision
  • Firmware revision
  • CAN / CANopen / RS485 interface selected
  • EDS / endpoint file matched to firmware
  • Encoder configuration
  • Brake / braking-resistor function
  • Connector and cable set
  • Current and speed limits
  • Customer controller requirements

docs.title: Controlled Drawing Reconciliation
docs.text:
A supplier-provided 2D assembly drawing labelled SG6010D has been checked against the published envelope. The 2D assembly source PDF is now published as a public engineering-reference copy. Its publication does not constitute approval as a revision-controlled manufacturing drawing.

The drawing confirms:

  • Total reduction ratio: 28.13:1
  • First-stage ratio: 9.67:1
  • Second-stage ratio: 2.908:1
  • Overall axial dimension: 58.77 mm nominal
  • Complete actuator weight: 791 g

The same drawing separates two operating tables:

  • Motor + second-stage reduction test: 100 +/-10 rpm rated speed, 170 +/-10 rpm no-load speed, 16 Nm rated torque and 50 Nm peak torque.
  • One controller-limited configuration: 60 +/-10 rpm rated speed, 170 +/-10 rpm no-load speed, 16 Nm rated torque and 45 Nm peak torque.

The second table is configuration-specific and must not replace the base mechanical test values for every SG-6010D order.

An original SG-6010D full assembly STEP is publicly downloadable (released 2026-11-18); it contains full assembly geometry.

docs.title: SG-6010HB Technical Datasheet v1.0
docs.text:
Status: Public engineering evaluation reference Online record: 2026-10-09 · Reference PDF: Rev0.1, 2026-11-19 Public source: Current SigGear product catalog

Download SG-6010HB Reference Datasheet PDF

The PDF summarizes the catalogue product, not an independently approved 2D/3D CAD envelope.

SG-6010HB is a compact planetary joint motor published by SigGear for exoskeleton joint applications. This datasheet consolidates the current catalog values without adding unpublished driver, encoder or interface claims.

docs.title: Key Performance
docs.text:
Parameter Published value Transmission structure Planetary structure Outer diameter 67.0 mm Product thickness 25.57 mm Reduction ratio 9.67:1 Backlash 15–20 arcmin Motor power 328 W Rated voltage 12–48 V Rated output speed 310 rpm No-load output speed 400 rpm Rated output torque 6 Nm Peak output torque 18 Nm Weight 298.5 g Allowable radial force 250 N Allowable axial force 100 N

Warning

Peak torque is not a continuous working rating. Peak duration, duty cycle and thermal suitability require application-specific confirmation.

A source-backed SG-6010HB Thermal Test Record is available. It records time from 30°C to 100°C at several torque levels under stall and 110 rpm load conditions; it does not by itself establish a continuous-duty thermal rating.

docs.title: Electrical and Motor Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Published value Phase damping 224 µΩ Phase inductance 235 µH Phase current full scale 33 A Rated bus current 12 A Static working bus current 0.08 A Motor structure 18N20P Motor torque constant 0.0606 Nm/A Thermistor 10 kΩ B3435 ±1% NTC B value 3435 Back EMF constant 0.0727 Vs/rad Motor KV value 104 KV (catalog notation)

Terminology note: “Phase damping” and “104 KV” are retained from the published catalog. Confirm the electrical definition and unit before using those two values in controller calculations.

docs.title: Published Application Positioning
docs.text:
The current SigGear catalog identifies SG-6010HB as an exoskeleton joint motor.

This identifies a real intended application direction; it does not mean the product is limited to exoskeletons or that every exoskeleton joint can use the same configuration.

docs.title: Mechanical Data Boundary
docs.text:
The supplied SG-6010HB 2D reference has been reviewed for its readable nominal mounting features. The separately supplied SG-6010HB exchange STEP was imported on 2026-11-19, but its full-assembly envelope still requires engineering reconciliation with the catalogue.

Public early-design information is summarized in the SG-6010HB Mechanical Interface, including the 67 mm envelope, 22.57 ±0.50 mm main body thickness, nominal 3.00 ±0.30 mm output-side extension, selected mounting patterns and wiring references.

The controlled production drawing and detailed internal assembly STEP remain request-only. No downloadable SG-6010HB STEP is approved; request configuration-matched exterior CAD and the current drawing revision before design freeze.

View Mechanical Interface View Thermal Test Record View Driver & Communication Request CAD / Drawing

docs.title: Driver-Equipped Configuration
docs.text:
SigGear has confirmed that the present driver-equipped SG-6010HB configuration uses the SG6010 driver platform documented in the current user manual.

Confirmed platform-level integration features include:

  • 15–48 V DC rated driver voltage
  • 16-bit single-turn absolute main encoder
  • CAN Simple
  • CANopen (CiA301 / CiA302 / CiA402)
  • RS485 / Modbus RTU with the corresponding interface configuration
  • Position, velocity, torque and MIT-style motion control
  • Type-C debugging / host communication
  • Second-encoder interface through I2C or UART

View Driver & Communication Reference

Note

The actuator catalog states 12–48 V, while the driver manual states 15–48 V DC rated driver operation and a 12 V minimum boundary. For the driver-equipped system, do not treat 12 V as a rated operating point without engineering confirmation.

Driver hardware revision, firmware, second-encoder hardware, cable / connector set, brake behavior and expansion interfaces must still be matched to the ordered configuration.

docs.title: SG-6010HB Driver and Communication Reference v1.0
docs.text:
Status: Public engineering integration reference Release date: 2026-10-09 Configuration boundary: Applies to the current driver-equipped SG-6010HB configuration using the confirmed SG6010 driver platform.

SigGear has confirmed that the SG6010 driver platform documented in the current SG6010 user manual applies to the present driver-equipped SG-6010HB configuration.

This page summarizes the integration information suitable for early engineering evaluation. Final driver hardware revision, firmware revision, cable set and ordered interface configuration must still be matched to the delivered unit.

docs.title: System Voltage Boundary
docs.text:
The mechanical actuator catalog and the driver manual use different voltage descriptions:

Item Published / confirmed value SG-6010HB catalog rated-voltage range 12–48 V Driver rated voltage 15–48 V DC Driver minimum / maximum voltage boundary 12 / 72 V DC

For a driver-equipped SG-6010HB system, do not treat the driver's 12 V minimum boundary as a rated continuous operating point.

Final power-supply selection should use the actual actuator configuration, required torque-speed point, driver revision and current limits.

docs.title: Driver Electrical Reference
docs.text:
Parameter Confirmed manual value Rated driver voltage 15–48 V DC Minimum / maximum driver voltage 12 / 72 V DC Rated current 6 A Maximum line current 30 A Maximum phase current 90 A Standby consumption <10 mA CAN maximum bitrate 1 Mbps USB Type-C rate 10 Mbps Main encoder resolution 16-bit single-turn absolute Driver operating temperature -20°C to 70°C Motor over-temperature alarm 90°C, adjustable Driver-board over-temperature alarm 90°C, adjustable

Warning

These are driver-platform values. They are not replacements for the SG-6010HB actuator torque, speed, thermal or duty-cycle limits.

docs.title: Confirmed Hardware Interfaces
docs.text:
The confirmed driver platform provides or supports:

  • Combined power + CAN connector
  • USB Type-C debugging / host communication
  • Main 16-bit single-turn absolute encoder
  • Second-encoder interface using I2C or UART
  • SWD programming / debugging interface
  • Motor NTC temperature input
  • Brake / braking-resistor interface
  • Minimum / maximum limit-switch inputs
  • Expansion interface for additional project-specific functions

The second-encoder interface does not mean that every SG-6010HB is supplied as a dual-encoder unit. The actual second encoder, mechanical mounting and firmware configuration must be confirmed for the ordered version.

docs.title: CAN Simple
docs.text:
The SG6010 driver manual documents a CAN Simple protocol with:

  • Standard CAN communication
  • Configurable node ID
  • Position command support
  • Velocity command support
  • Torque command support
  • Current / velocity limit settings
  • Periodic message configuration
  • MIT-style motion-control commands

The manual documents a maximum CAN bitrate of 1 Mbps.

Final node ID, bitrate, command scaling and firmware revision should be confirmed before controller integration.

docs.title: CANopen
docs.text:
The confirmed driver platform includes CANopen support.

The manual states implementation against:

  • CiA301
  • CiA302
  • CiA402

The documented CANopen implementation includes the CiA402 servo state machine and operating modes including position-, velocity- and torque-related servo modes.

A matching EDS / object-dictionary revision should be supplied for the delivered firmware when CANopen is selected.

docs.title: RS485 / Modbus RTU
docs.text:
The SG6010 manual contains an RS485 communication section using Modbus RTU.

The documented implementation states:

  • Maximum communication speed: 115200 bps
  • Factory default communication speed: 115200 bps
  • Standard Modbus RTU register operations are documented

RS485 hardware availability depends on the supplied interface / expansion configuration. Confirm the actual connector and hardware version before final integration.

docs.title: Control Modes
docs.text:
The driver manual documents four main control families:

  • Position control
  • Velocity control
  • Torque control
  • Motion control / MIT-style control

Additional documented control behaviors include:

docs.title: Position
docs.text:
• Filtered Position Control
  • Trajectory / trapezoidal position control
  • Circular Position Control

docs.title: Velocity
docs.text:
• Direct Velocity Control
  • Ramped Velocity Control

docs.title: Torque
docs.text:
• Direct Torque Control
  • Ramped Torque Control

docs.title: MIT-Style Motion Control
docs.text:
Motion control combines position, velocity and torque terms.

The manual notes an important integration distinction: USB-side commands and CAN MIT protocol commands may use different reference-side conventions. Controller integration should therefore follow the exact protocol definition for the delivered firmware rather than assuming that all command channels use the same coordinate convention.

docs.title: Encoder and Feedback
docs.text:
The confirmed driver platform specifies a:

16-bit single-turn absolute main encoder

A second-encoder interface is available through:

  • I2C
  • UART

The second encoder is a configurable interface capability, not a universal statement that every delivered SG-6010HB includes two physical encoders.

docs.title: Temperature and Protection
docs.text:
The driver platform supports:

  • Motor NTC temperature input
  • Motor temperature alarm: 90°C adjustable
  • Driver-board temperature alarm: 90°C adjustable
  • Configurable current limit
  • Configurable speed limit

The driver manual also documents temperature-dependent current limiting.

These protection functions do not replace application-specific thermal validation.

View SG-6010HB Thermal Test Record

docs.title: Expansion Interface Boundary
docs.text:
The driver platform documentation describes an expansion interface capable of supporting additional functions / protocols such as:

  • RS485
  • EtherCAT
  • SPI / USART / I2C / PWM / ADC / GPIO based expansion
  • Pulse / direction and other project-specific interfaces

EtherCAT is not presented here as a standard SG-6010HB interface. It remains subject to expansion hardware, firmware and project confirmation.

docs.title: Integration Checklist
docs.text:
Before final integration, confirm:

  • Driver hardware revision
  • Firmware revision
  • Power-supply voltage and current capability
  • CAN / CANopen / RS485 interface selected
  • CAN bitrate and node-ID plan
  • CANopen EDS / object dictionary revision
  • Main / second encoder configuration
  • Connector and cable set
  • Motor and driver temperature thresholds
  • Current and speed limits
  • Brake / braking-resistor configuration
  • Customer controller architecture
  • Whether an expansion interface such as EtherCAT is required

Request Integration Files

docs.title: SG-6010HB Thermal Test Record v1.0
docs.text:
Status: Public engineering test record Release date: 2026-10-09 Source: Internal SG-6010HB temperature-rise test worksheet supplied for engineering documentation

This page publishes only the test values that are clearly identifiable in the source worksheet.

It is not a continuous-duty rating, thermal certification, lifetime statement or replacement for application-specific validation.

docs.title: What the Source Records
docs.text:
The worksheet contains two test sections:

  1. Stall condition — time from 30°C to 100°C
  2. 110 rpm load condition — time from 30°C to 100°C

The source does not identify the exact temperature sensor location in the table heading, so this page does not label the 100°C threshold as winding temperature, housing temperature, PCB temperature or another specific measurement point.

docs.title: Stall Condition — 30°C to 100°C
docs.text:
Applied torque Recorded time to 100°C 6.0 Nm 929.68 s 10 Nm 113.61 s 15 Nm 10.72 s 20 Nm 5 s 25 Nm No time value recorded 30 Nm No time value recorded

The source worksheet also contains the note “Peak 21 Nm” in this section.

This note is not used as a published SG-6010HB peak-torque specification because the worksheet does not define the note sufficiently and the current public product specification remains 18 Nm peak torque.

docs.title: 110 rpm Load Condition — 30°C to 100°C
docs.text:
Applied torque Recorded time to 100°C 6.0 Nm 578 s 10 Nm 42 s 15 Nm 12 s 20 Nm 5 s 25 Nm No time value recorded 30 Nm No time value recorded

The source labels this section as a 110 rpm load temperature-rise test.

The 110 rpm value is a test condition only. It does not replace the currently published SG-6010HB rated output speed of 310 rpm.

docs.title: Source Fields Not Interpreted Publicly
docs.text:
The worksheet contains additional fields that are not sufficiently defined for safe public engineering use:

  • A repeated multi-value temperature text field without sensor names or point mapping.
  • A dynamometer voltage column with values 0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55 and 0.65 for several rows, but no unit or calibration definition.

These values are therefore not converted into product specifications, efficiency values, electrical voltage claims or thermal-channel labels.

docs.title: Engineering Interpretation Boundary
docs.text:
The test record supports a limited statement:

Under the recorded test setup, the time for the monitored temperature channel to rise from 30°C to 100°C became much shorter as applied torque increased.

It does not by itself establish:

  • continuous allowable torque
  • continuous duty cycle
  • allowable peak duration
  • winding temperature limit
  • housing temperature limit
  • thermal resistance
  • thermal time constant
  • safe operating area
  • lifetime at temperature
  • exoskeleton duty-cycle suitability

Those items require a defined test setup, sensor location, cooling condition, ambient condition, mounting condition and acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Use for Project Evaluation
docs.text:
For an exoskeleton or compact joint project, use this record as supporting thermal evidence only.

Final selection should still define:

  • continuous joint torque
  • peak torque and peak duration
  • speed profile
  • duty cycle
  • ambient temperature
  • mounting heat path
  • enclosure / airflow condition
  • driver current limits
  • motor and driver temperature protection
  • required thermal margin
