docs.title: SigGear Knowledge Base
docs.text: This knowledge base is the controlled public information layer for SigGear products, applications, selection guidance and company information. It is designed for customers, distributors, sales staff, engineers and AI-assisted retrieval.

docs.title: Find Information Quickly
docs.text: Need Start here Find a specific product model Product model index Understand the structured product records Product data dictionary Check what sales may state or must confirm Sales usage and review status Qualify and respond to an inquiry Sales and inquiry guides Compare published products Product overview Choose a product for an application Application guides Prepare engineering requirements Selection guides Understand product terms and units Terminology and units Answer common technical and sales questions Product and engineering FAQ Check whether a statement can be published Documentation policy Add or update information Update and review workflow

docs.title: Recommended Search Method
docs.text:
Use the search box with the most specific identifier available:

  • Model number, such as SG-6010D, CPM-80-25 or SG-2878
  • Product family, such as cycloidal joint module or planetary gearbox
  • Application, such as humanoid knee, robot gripper or AGV wheel drive
  • Requirement, such as rated torque, radial load, CAN or backdrivability

Search results should lead to a canonical product page, application guide, selection guide or controlled FAQ answer. When two pages appear to conflict, do not select the more favorable value. Follow the conflict process in the documentation policy.

docs.title: Source-of-Truth Boundaries
docs.text:
• A canonical product page is the authoritative public page for one published model or series.
  • A controlled engineering drawing, released specification or approved test record remains the technical source behind the public page.
  • A quotation and technical agreement define the configuration supplied to a specific customer.
  • Product-family and application pages provide navigation and selection guidance; they do not override a model page.

docs.title: Public Repository Boundary
docs.text: This repository is public. It must not contain customer identities, customer drawings, private quotations, internal costs, supplier details, credentials, unreleased product data, NDA material or restricted test records. Store those materials only in an approved private system.

docs.title: Current Coverage
docs.text:
The knowledge base currently covers:

  • Integrated planetary robot joint actuators
  • Integrated cycloidal joint modules
  • Planetary gearboxes from 6 mm to 42 mm
  • Micro gear motor solution families
  • Flat BLDC motor and joint-drive solution families
  • Hub gear motors
  • Robotics, medical, laboratory, instrument and automation applications

Coverage will expand only after the corresponding technical data and public claims have been reviewed.

docs.title: SigGear Documentation Policy
docs.text: This policy defines what can be published, how technical claims are supported and which page wins when information differs.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The documentation must be accurate enough for preliminary product selection, clear enough for international customers and structured enough for reliable human and AI retrieval. It must not expose confidential business or customer information.

docs.title: Source Hierarchy
docs.text:
Use the highest available source in this order:

  1. Released model-specific specification or controlled engineering drawing
  2. Approved model- and configuration-specific test report
  3. Current certificate or third-party verification document within its stated scope
  4. Written engineering confirmation identifying the exact model and configuration
  5. Approved product catalog derived from the sources above

Sales messages, marketplace listings, competitor pages, customer statements and AI-generated text are not technical sources of truth.

docs.title: Claim Classes
docs.text: Class Example Publication requirement Model-specific specification Torque, speed, ratio, dimensions, load rating Exact model, unit, source and configuration scope verified Configuration-dependent function Driver, encoder, CAN, RS485, EtherCAT, brake Included hardware and firmware scope stated; optional functions labeled Test-based performance Noise, temperature rise, efficiency, service life Test method, sample configuration and conditions available Certification claim ISO, IATF, EMC or product conformity Holder, scope, standard and applicable models checked General engineering guidance Selection factors and definitions Written as guidance, not as a guaranteed product result

docs.title: Canonical Page Rules
docs.text:
• Each published model or series has one canonical product page.
  • Index, application and FAQ pages link to the canonical page instead of creating an independent specification source.
  • Summary tables may repeat a small number of selection values, but they must link to the canonical page and be updated in the same pull request.
  • A family-level statement must not be applied automatically to every model.
  • Optional functions must be labeled optional, project-specific or subject to configuration confirmation.

docs.title: Conflict Handling
docs.text:
When two sources or pages disagree:

  1. Stop publication of the disputed value.
  2. Record the exact model, field, values and source revisions in a Product Data Update issue.
  3. Ask the responsible engineering or product role to identify the current controlled source.
  4. Update every affected summary and canonical page in one change.
  5. Preserve the decision in the issue or pull request history.

Do not average conflicting values, choose the newest-looking file automatically or publish the more favorable claim.

docs.title: Public and Private Content Boundary
docs.text:
This public repository may contain approved product information, application guidance, selection guidance, public company facts and public contact information.

It must not contain:

  • Customer names, addresses, messages, requirements or drawings without explicit publication approval
  • Prices, discounts, payment terms, internal MOQ rules or internal quotation strategy
  • Internal costs, margins, supplier identities or purchasing records
  • Unreleased models, uncontrolled drawings or confidential test reports
  • NDA-controlled files, credentials, API keys or private system links
  • Personal telephone numbers or messaging accounts without explicit approval

docs.title: AI-Assisted Writing Rule
docs.text: AI can organize, translate, summarize and check documentation, but it must not invent product values, fill missing specifications, infer compatibility or convert an optional feature into a standard claim. Every technical value still requires an approved human-verifiable source.

docs.title: Language Rule
docs.text: The public documentation language is English. Use the model spelling, terminology and units defined in the glossary. Write concise factual statements and distinguish confirmed specifications from selection guidance.

docs.title: SigGear Terminology and Units
docs.text: Use these terms consistently across product pages, quotations, emails and technical discussions. A model-specific definition or test condition takes priority when explicitly stated.

docs.title: Product Terms
docs.text: Term Controlled meaning Robot joint actuator A motor and transmission assembly for a robot joint; encoder and driver inclusion must be stated separately Integrated joint module A compact joint assembly combining multiple drive components; list the included motor, reducer, encoder, driver and brake explicitly Precision planetary gearhead Preferred SigGear international product term for the standalone 8–42 mm precision planetary reduction unit; select by model and configuration Planetary gearbox Engineering synonym for planetary gearhead; also retained in historical page URLs, CAD paths and legacy search terminology Micro Planetary Gearheads Published SigGear diameter class 8–16 mm: 8P, 10P, 12P, 14P and 16P Miniature Planetary Gearheads Published SigGear diameter class 20–32 mm: 20P, 22P, 24P, 28P and 32P Compact Planetary Gearheads Published SigGear diameter class 36–42 mm: 36P and 42P Gearhead Only A gearhead supplied for OEM integration with a customer-selected motor, subject to interface and operating-point review Motor + Gearhead Assembly A motor-matched gearhead drive assembled or evaluated for a specified project; exact inclusions must be confirmed Cycloidal joint module A joint-drive assembly using a cycloidal pinwheel transmission Micro gear motor A compact motor and gearbox assembly; motor type, diameter, ratio and feedback must be identified for a specific selection Hub gear motor A geared motor arranged for compact wheel or hub-drive integration Standard configuration The published baseline configuration for a model; it does not include optional functions unless stated Customer-specific configuration A configuration defined by a quotation, drawing or technical agreement for one project

docs.title: Naming and Legacy Link Policy
docs.text: Use Gearhead as the primary product naming convention for newly updated English product copy, title tags, model directories, application guides and inquiry labels. Keep planetary gearbox as a useful alternate search term in explanatory content. Never rename a published URL path, public CAD filename, TraceParts link, or existing request parameter solely for terminology consistency. Model-specific ratings and released engineering drawings remain the source of truth.

docs.title: Performance Terms
docs.text: Term Controlled meaning Rated torque Output torque permitted under defined continuous or duty-rated conditions Peak torque Short-duration output torque subject to current, thermal and duty-cycle limits Holding torque Torque available while maintaining position under specified control and thermal conditions; not interchangeable with rated torque Rated speed Output speed associated with the stated rated operating point No-load speed Output speed measured without external working load under stated electrical conditions Reduction ratio Input speed divided by output speed, expressed as ratio:1 Backlash Lost angular motion during direction reversal under a defined measurement method and load Repeatability Ability to return to the same position under repeated stated conditions Accuracy Difference between commanded or indicated position and actual position under a defined method Radial load Load acting perpendicular to the output axis Axial load Load acting along the output axis Overturning moment Bending moment applied to the output bearing or mounting structure Duty cycle Relationship between operating time, load states and rest time over a complete cycle Backdrivability Ability of an external output load to drive the mechanism backward under defined conditions

docs.title: Electrical and Control Terms
docs.text: Term Controlled meaning Operating voltage Permitted supply-voltage range for the confirmed configuration Rated current Current associated with a defined rated operating point; distinguish bus current from phase current Encoder Position-sensing device; state whether it measures motor-side or output-side position and whether it is incremental or absolute Driver Power electronics and control hardware used to commutate and control the motor FOC Field-oriented control for a suitable motor and feedback configuration CAN Controller Area Network physical/data-link technology; protocol and command set still require confirmation RS485 Differential serial physical layer; baud rate and application protocol require confirmation EtherCAT Industrial Ethernet fieldbus; availability must be confirmed for the selected driver and firmware Closed-loop control Control using measured feedback; identify the controlled variable, feedback location and loop implementation

docs.title: Preferred Units and Formatting
docs.text:
Quantity Preferred unit Example Torque Nm 25 Nm Speed rpm 120 rpm Power W 500 W Voltage VDC 24–48 VDC Current A 12 A Diameter and length mm 80 mm Mass below 1 kg g 430 g Mass at or above 1 kg kg 1.2 kg Backlash arcmin 5–10 arcmin Radial and axial force N 500 N Temperature °C 25 °C

Use a space between a number and its unit. Use an en dash for ranges. Do not mix output-side and motor-side values without labeling them.

docs.title: SigGear Product Data Dictionary
docs.text: SigGear product master-data records provide a machine-readable inventory of the claims already published on canonical product pages. They support GitHub search, AI-assisted retrieval and automated consistency checks.

docs.title: Record Location
docs.text: Product records are stored in data/products/. One YAML file represents one published model or series.

docs.title: Record Fields
docs.text: Field Meaning schema_version Version of the record structure record_id Stable lowercase identifier matching the YAML filename record_type model or series model Official model number for a model record display_name Human-readable product or series name product_family Controlled product-family identifier canonical_page Unique public page for the model or series public_page_status Publication state of the canonical page record_status Status of the structured inventory record configuration_summary Boundary statement for included or configuration-dependent components published_specifications Exact public value strings mirrored from the canonical page sales_usage Permitted preliminary use, confirmation requirements and prohibited shortcuts technical_review Public inventory status and boundary for non-public source or approval records source_control Public claim source and handling of non-public technical sources cad_control Non-sensitive CAD / drawing source status, including approved drawing reference code and whether detailed assembly CAD is public or request-only inventory_checked_on Date the record was compared with the public page

docs.title: Status Meanings
docs.text:
public_page_status: published means the canonical page is publicly available. It does not replace a quotation or technical agreement.

record_status: published_inventory means the YAML record mirrors the current public page. It does not independently certify the engineering value.

technical_source_status: not_recorded_in_public_repository means drawings, test records or internal approvals are intentionally not stored in this public repository. It does not mean that no technical source exists.

docs.title: Exact-String Rule
docs.text:
Values in published_specifications preserve the text shown on the canonical page, including ranges, tolerances and units. For example, 24–48 VDC must not be silently changed to 48 V or converted into a different rating.

The automated validator checks that every recorded value still appears on its canonical page. If a page specification changes, the corresponding YAML record must change in the same pull request.

docs.title: Configuration Boundaries
docs.text:
The product record must not turn an optional function into a standard claim. Driver, encoder, brake, CAN, RS485, EtherCAT and control-mode availability remain configuration-specific unless the canonical model page explicitly states otherwise.

The sales_usage block identifies what may be used for preliminary selection and which topics must be confirmed before quotation or final model approval. A prohibited item is a shortcut that must never be taken, such as treating peak torque as continuous torque or promising an optional interface as standard.

docs.title: Technical Review Boundary
docs.text:
technical_review.public_inventory_status: complete means the current public page has been inventoried into the YAML record. It does not mean that this GitHub review performed engineering approval.

Controlled source documents, approval records and reviewer identities remain outside the public repository unless SigGear explicitly approves a non-sensitive reference code for publication. A product record may store that approved reference code and the review date without publishing the underlying controlled drawing. next_internal_action describes the reconciliation or revision-control work that remains.

docs.title: CAD Control Boundary
docs.text:
When cad_control is present:

  • controlled_2d_drawing records only the approved non-sensitive drawing identifier.
  • full_assembly_step_status records whether detailed assembly CAD has been reviewed and how it may be supplied.
  • public_raw_assembly_step: false means the full internal assembly is not a public download.
  • public_raw_assembly_step: true means a full-assembly STEP is published at public_full_assembly_step_path; its source revision and engineering approval remain separate review records.

The structured record does not contain the controlled drawing or full assembly CAD itself.

docs.title: Source Boundary
docs.text: These records contain public product data and non-sensitive source-control metadata only. Customer files, prices, internal costs, supplier information, unreleased products, private drawings, restricted test reports and NDA material must not be added.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run:

python scripts/validate_product_data.py

The check verifies required fields, unique identifiers, canonical-page coverage and exact published-claim synchronization.

docs.title: SigGear Product and Engineering FAQ
docs.text: These answers provide controlled public guidance. Model-specific pages, quotations and technical agreements take priority over general answers.

docs.title: What is an integrated robot joint actuator?
docs.text: An integrated robot joint actuator combines a motor and precision transmission in a compact joint package. Depending on the selected SigGear model and configuration, the assembly may also include an encoder, driver and communication interface. Do not assume that every product includes every component.

docs.title: Can SigGear supply a joint actuator without an integrated driver?
docs.text: Selected models can be supplied with or without an integrated driver. The sensor, cable, connector and control configuration must be confirmed in the quotation.

docs.title: Do SigGear joint actuators support CAN, RS485 or EtherCAT?
docs.text: Communication capability is configuration-specific. Some driver-equipped products support CAN. RS485, EtherCAT and other interfaces may be optional or project-specific and must not be described as standard unless the selected product page, quotation and technical agreement confirm them.

docs.title: Can the actuator control position, velocity and torque?
docs.text: Available control modes depend on the driver, encoder, firmware and product configuration. Confirm the required modes, protocol, command set, feedback signals and controller limits during engineering review.

docs.title: How should rated torque and peak torque be interpreted?
docs.text: Rated torque is associated with sustained operation under defined electrical, thermal and duty-cycle conditions. Peak torque is a short-duration capability. Its permitted duration depends on voltage, current limit, cooling, installation, ambient temperature and motion cycle. Peak torque must not be used as a continuous rating.

docs.title: Should a planetary or cycloidal transmission be selected?
docs.text: There is no universal choice. Compare the complete torque-speed cycle, allowable size and weight, backlash, external loads, efficiency, thermal conditions, shock loads, output speed, control architecture and project cost. Use the published model pages as starting points and confirm the final selection with complete application data.

docs.title: Is a gearbox or actuator backdrivable?
docs.text: Backdrivability depends on the complete motor, transmission ratio, friction, seals, preload, mechanism, controller state and applied load. It must not be assumed from the product family alone. State the required power-off behavior and manual force or torque during selection.

docs.title: Are noise and service-life values available?
docs.text: Noise and service life depend on model, ratio, speed, load, duty cycle, lubrication, mounting and test method. Numeric claims are supplied only when applicable data is available for the selected configuration. A product video is not a substitute for a controlled acoustic test.

docs.title: Can SigGear provide CAD models and detailed drawings?
docs.text: STEP models, 2D drawings and detailed interface documents are provided after application review and inquiry. The supplied file must match the quoted model and configuration.

docs.title: What customization can SigGear evaluate?
docs.text: Depending on engineering feasibility and project scope, SigGear can evaluate motor-and-reducer matching, reduction ratio, output shaft, flange, housing, cable, connector, encoder, driver, communication, branding, labeling and packaging changes. Availability, engineering cost, lead time and minimum quantity are confirmed case by case.

docs.title: What information is needed for product selection or quotation?
docs.text:
Provide at least:

  • Application and axis position
  • Continuous torque
  • Peak torque and peak duration
  • Rated and maximum output speed
  • Operating voltage
  • Outer-diameter, thickness, length and weight limits
  • Radial, axial and overturning loads
  • Duty cycle, ambient temperature and cooling method
  • Backlash, positioning and repeatability requirements
  • Encoder, driver, communication and brake requirements
  • Prototype quantity and estimated annual quantity

For robot arms, humanoids, quadrupeds and exoskeletons, prepare a separate requirement set for every joint axis.

docs.title: Does a public product page replace a quotation or technical agreement?
docs.text: No. Public pages support preliminary selection. The quotation and technical agreement define the ordered model, configuration, included components, interfaces, performance scope and commercial terms.

docs.title: SigGear Knowledge Base Update and Review Workflow
docs.text: Use this workflow for new models, specification changes, new application pages, corrected claims and documentation maintenance.

docs.title: Content Status
docs.text: Status Meaning Proposed A change request exists but source material has not been confirmed Technical review Engineering or product owner is checking model, configuration, values and evidence Content review Technical facts are fixed; English, structure, links and terminology are being checked Publish ready Required reviews and automated checks are complete Published The change is merged to main and deployed Superseded A newer controlled page or revision replaces the old information

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Responsibility Requester Describes the change and supplies the source file or exact source reference Technical reviewer Confirms the model, configuration, values, units, test conditions and claim scope Content reviewer Checks English, terminology, search terms, navigation, cross-links and confidentiality Maintainer Confirms automated checks, merges the pull request and verifies deployment

One person may perform more than one role, but technical review must be explicit for model-specific claims.

docs.title: Update Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open a Product Data Update issue.
  2. Identify the model, product family, requested change and affected pages.
  3. Cite the controlled source, including document name, revision and date when available.
  4. Confirm that the source is approved for public use.
  5. Update the canonical product page first.
  6. Update every summary table, application page, FAQ or index that repeats the changed information.
  7. Use the model spelling, terminology and units in the glossary.
  8. Run the documentation validator and strict MkDocs build.
  9. Obtain technical and content review in the pull request.
  10. Merge to main and verify the deployed page and search result.

docs.title: New Product Page Minimum Content
docs.text:
A new model page should include:

  • Exact model name and product type
  • Product overview without unsupported superlatives
  • Included and optional configuration boundaries
  • Key specifications with units
  • Rated and peak conditions where applicable
  • Mechanical, electrical, encoder, driver and communication sections as applicable
  • External-load and thermal limitations where supported
  • Product images with descriptive alternative text
  • Application guidance
  • Inquiry information and links to related pages

Missing data must be omitted or clearly marked as requiring confirmation. Do not estimate it from a similar model.

docs.title: Search and Retrieval Checklist
docs.text:
• Use the official model number in the H1 heading and body.
  • Include common product-family and application terms naturally.
  • Link the model from the product model index.
  • Add the page to mkdocs.yml navigation.
  • Link to related product, application and selection pages.
  • Avoid duplicate pages targeting the same model and intent.

docs.title: Required Checks
docs.text:
Run locally before review:

python scripts/validate_docs.py
mkdocs build --strict

The pull-request workflow repeats these checks automatically.

docs.title: Urgent Corrections
docs.text:
For a safety-relevant, materially misleading or confidential disclosure:

  1. Remove or correct the public statement as the immediate priority.
  2. Record the reason and affected pages.
  3. Complete technical review before adding a replacement claim.
  4. Check cached summaries and other pages for the same statement.

docs.title: Flat BLDC Motors and Joint Drives
Product Overview
docs.text:
SigGear supplies flat motor and integrated joint-drive solutions for robots, exoskeletons and compact automation systems.

The standard flat joint-drive families are distinguished by their transmission structure:

  • SigGear-Horse: planetary transmission core
  • SigGear-Tiger: cycloidal-pinwheel transmission core

These products are intended for applications that require a short axial package and integrated mechanical and electrical functions. Final motor, reducer, driver, encoder and communication configurations are confirmed for the selected model and quotation.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
SG-2878 is a 99 mm hub gear motor using a planetary reduction structure. Compared with SG-2877, it provides higher rated and peak torque for AGV, AMR, mobile robots, rehabilitation platforms and compact wheel-drive systems.

The standard catalog configuration uses Hall sensors. An external motor controller is required unless a controller is specifically included in the quotation.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
SigGear develops miniature gear-motor and compact transmission solutions for robotics, medical devices, laboratory automation, precision instruments and compact industrial mechanisms.

The product range is based on miniature planetary gear reducers and application-specific motor integration. Available gearbox diameters and final motor configurations depend on the required torque, speed, voltage, installation envelope and production quantity.

  • Compact planetary reduction motors
  • Motor and gearbox integration based on the 8–42 mm planetary reducer range
  • Custom output shafts, flanges and mounting interfaces
  • Optional encoder, brake, cable and connector integration after engineering review
  • Application-specific OEM and ODM development

  • Medical and dental devices

docs.title: Motor Integration
docs.text:
Depending on the selected gearbox and project requirements, SigGear can evaluate integration with:

  • Brushed DC motors
  • Brushless DC motors
  • Stepper motors
  • Servo motors
  • Customer-specified motors

Motor compatibility is confirmed according to input speed, power, shaft interface, duty cycle, thermal conditions and required output performance.

docs.title: Start Even If the Ratio Is Not Defined
docs.text:
A project can start from the mechanism rather than a complete gearbox specification. If the reduction ratio is unknown, provide the motor speed and desired output speed if available. If the output torque is unknown, send the load, mechanism geometry or a sketch so the engineering team can identify what must be calculated or tested.

docs.title: SigGear Sales and Inquiry Knowledge
docs.text: This section provides a controlled public workflow for qualifying customer requirements, selecting a preliminary product candidate and preparing a safe response. It is intended for sales staff, distributors and AI-assisted inquiry handling.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Stage Purpose Guide 1. Qualify Collect the minimum information needed to understand the project Customer qualification checklist 2. Match Compare the requirement with canonical SigGear product pages Product matching workflow 3. Respond Answer the customer first, state boundaries and request missing information Inquiry response policy 4. Draft Use a controlled structure without inventing parameters or commercial terms Reply templates 5. Quote Confirm technical and commercial readiness before issuing a formal quotation Quotation readiness checklist

docs.title: Core Rule
docs.text:
A public product page supports preliminary selection. It does not by itself authorize a final technical commitment, price, delivery time, customization promise or production release.

Use the product model index, machine-readable product records and sales usage review matrix together.

docs.title: Public and Private Boundary
docs.text:
This public repository may contain generic inquiry questions, response structures and approved public product information.

Do not add:

  • Customer names, addresses, contact details, messages or drawings
  • Customer-specific requirements that could identify a project
  • Prices, discounts, internal MOQ rules, costs or margins
  • Private quotations, payment terms or negotiation strategy
  • Unreleased product data, restricted drawings or NDA material

Customer-specific work belongs in an approved private project or customer-management system.

docs.title: Sales Contact
docs.text: Wanrong Wang International Sales, SigGear wangwanrong@siggear.com

docs.title: SigGear Customer Qualification Checklist
docs.text: Ask enough questions to identify a real application and avoid recommending a product from one attractive parameter alone. Start with the minimum questions and add detail according to the customer's technical level.

docs.title: Five Essential Questions
docs.text:
1. What type of robot or equipment are you developing?
  2. What continuous torque, peak torque and output speed do you need?
  3. Do you prefer an integrated actuator or a separate gearbox and motor?
  4. What are your estimated prototype quantity and annual quantity?
  5. What is the main problem with your current solution or supplier?

Suggested English wording:

What type of robot or equipment are you currently developing? What continuous torque, peak torque and output speed do you need? Do you prefer an integrated actuator or a separate gearbox and motor? What is your estimated prototype quantity and annual quantity? What is the main problem with your current solution or supplier?

docs.title: Engineering Requirements
docs.text:
Collect the following before final selection:

  • Application and exact axis or installation position
  • Concept, prototype, validation or mass-production stage
  • Continuous torque
  • Peak torque and peak duration
  • Rated and maximum output speed
  • Acceleration, deceleration and complete motion cycle
  • Operating voltage and available current
  • Maximum outer diameter, thickness, length and weight
  • Radial, axial and overturning loads
  • Backlash, accuracy and repeatability targets
  • Duty cycle, ambient temperature and cooling method
  • Noise, vibration and service-life targets
  • Required encoder, driver, brake and power-off behavior
  • CAN, RS485, EtherCAT or other communication requirement
  • Required control modes and protocol
  • CAD, drawing, datasheet or test-data requirement

For a robot with multiple joints, collect a separate requirement set for every axis.

docs.title: Project and Decision Information
docs.text:
• Company name, country and website
  • Current supplier or current drive architecture, when the customer is willing to share it
  • Main technical or commercial pain point
  • Expected supplier-selection date
  • Prototype deadline and production target
  • Technical decision maker and purchasing contact
  • Prototype quantity and estimated annual quantity
  • Delivery country or destination for freight evaluation
  • Preferred communication method

docs.title: Simplified Questions for a Non-Technical Contact
docs.text:
If the customer appears to be an owner, buyer or early-stage founder, begin with:

  1. What will the motor, gearbox or actuator be used for?
  2. What torque and speed do you need, if known?
  3. What is the maximum product size?
  4. What voltage will the equipment use?
  5. How many pieces do you need for the first order?
  6. Where should the order be delivered?
  7. What is the easiest way to contact you?

Do not send a long technical questionnaire before answering the customer's first question. Ask the smallest useful set, then continue after the customer responds.

docs.title: Qualification Outcome
docs.text:
Classify the inquiry as one of the following:

  • Standard candidate identified: published model is a reasonable starting point.
  • Engineering review required: customization or configuration confirmation is necessary.
  • Insufficient information: required torque, speed, size or architecture is missing.
  • No published match: the requirement is outside the current public product range.

docs.title: SigGear Inquiry Response Policy
docs.text: This policy defines the order, evidence and language used in customer replies.

docs.title: Response Order
docs.text:
1. Answer the customer's explicit question with confirmed information.
  2. State which product or family may be a preliminary candidate.
  3. Explain any configuration or evidence boundary.
  4. Ask for the smallest useful set of missing requirements.
  5. Request the preferred contact method when useful.
  6. State the next action, such as engineering review, model confirmation or quotation preparation.

Do not begin with a ten-minute company introduction or a long questionnaire.

docs.title: Short Company Introduction
docs.text:
Use only after the customer's application is understood:

We are SigGear, a Chinese manufacturer specializing in precision reducers and integrated robot joint actuators. Our joint modules can integrate the motor, reducer, encoder and driver, and we also support customized planetary and cycloidal solutions for robotic applications.

The wording “can integrate” is intentional. It does not mean that every model automatically includes a driver, encoder or every communication interface.

docs.title: Information Sources
docs.text:
Use information in this order:

  1. Canonical model page
  2. Matching product master-data record
  3. Sales usage and technical review status
  4. Application and selection guides
  5. Private engineering confirmation for the exact quoted configuration

If two sources conflict, stop and open a product-data review. Do not choose the more favorable value.

docs.title: Claim Rules
docs.text:
• Distinguish continuous torque from peak torque and request peak duration.
  • State whether the driver and encoder are included, optional or external.
  • Confirm CAN, RS485, EtherCAT, PID and control modes for the selected electronics and firmware.
  • Do not promise noise, life, efficiency, thermal or backdrivability values without applicable evidence and conditions.
  • Do not claim certification beyond the certificate holder, scope, model and standard.
  • Do not describe a product video as a controlled noise test.
  • Do not describe a preliminary candidate as a perfect match.

docs.title: Price, Lead Time and Customization
docs.text:
Do not invent or reuse a price, discount, MOQ, tooling fee or lead time from another project. Before a formal quotation, confirm:

  • Exact model and configuration
  • Prototype and production quantity
  • Customization scope
  • Required documents and testing
  • Delivery destination
  • Payment and shipping terms through the approved private process

For a custom request, state that feasibility, engineering cost and lead time are subject to technical review.

docs.title: Reply Style
docs.text:
• Use simple English for a buyer or company owner.
  • Use structured technical detail for an engineer.
  • Answer first, then list the information required from the customer.
  • Use bullets for parameters and questions.
  • State uncertainty directly and define how it will be confirmed.
  • Never expose another customer's project, price or drawing as evidence.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: Wanrong Wang International Sales, SigGear wangwanrong@siggear.com

docs.title: SigGear Product Matching Workflow
docs.text: Use this workflow to create a preliminary shortlist. Do not describe a product as a perfect match until the complete requirement and ordered configuration have been reviewed.

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the Required Architecture
docs.text: Customer need Starting product family Motor, reducer, encoder and driver in one compact robot joint Robot joint actuators Compact high-torque joint using cycloidal transmission Cycloidal joint modules Separate precision reducer for integration with a motor Planetary gearboxes Miniature motor and gearbox assembly Micro gear motors Flat motor or short-axial joint drive Flat BLDC motors and joint drives Compact wheel or hub drive Hub gear motors

docs.title: Step 2: Screen Torque and Speed
docs.text:
Compare continuous torque with rated torque. Compare the customer's required peak torque together with peak duration, current limit, duty cycle and cooling.

Never use peak torque as the only selection value. A candidate must satisfy the complete torque-speed cycle.

docs.title: Step 3: Screen Mechanical Integration
docs.text:
Check:

  • Outer diameter, thickness, length and mass
  • Reduction ratio
  • Mounting interface and shaft
  • Radial, axial and overturning loads
  • Backlash, accuracy and repeatability
  • Shock, impact and structural conditions

External loads must be reviewed separately from output torque. Significant cantilevered or tendon loads may require additional bearing support.

docs.title: Step 4: Screen Electrical and Control Requirements
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • Operating voltage and current limits
  • Driver inclusion
  • Encoder or Hall-sensor configuration
  • Position, velocity and torque-control requirements
  • CAN, RS485, EtherCAT or other interface
  • Protocol, baud rate, command set and feedback data
  • Brake, holding and power-off behavior

An interface name alone does not confirm protocol compatibility.

docs.title: Step 5: Screen Environment and Validation Needs
docs.text: Check duty cycle, ambient temperature, cooling, ingress protection, noise, vibration, service life and required test evidence. Do not transfer a product-level IP rating to the complete customer machine.

docs.title: Step 6: Screen Project Readiness
docs.text: Confirm prototype quantity, annual forecast, project stage, selection date, required documents and delivery destination. These inputs affect configuration, engineering review, quotation and freight evaluation.

docs.title: Standard Candidate
docs.text: A canonical public model is a reasonable starting point and no unconfirmed modification is required. The quotation must still state the exact configuration.

docs.title: Configured Standard Product
docs.text: The mechanical model may be standard, but driver, encoder, cable, connector, communication or firmware must be selected and confirmed.

docs.title: Custom Engineering Project
docs.text: The customer requires a changed ratio, shaft, interface, housing, electronics or performance target. Engineering feasibility, development scope, cost and lead time require separate review.

docs.title: No Published Match
docs.text: State this clearly. Do not force-fit the closest model or invent an unreleased solution.

docs.title: Final Check
docs.text: Before recommending a model, read its canonical product page and the sales usage and review status. If the requirement conflicts with a prohibited shortcut, stop and request engineering review.

docs.title: Engineering Guides
docs.text:
Find a Planetary Gearbox: Motor RPM → Published Ratio / Rated Torque → PDF / STEP

Or use the 8–42 mm model catalogue and STEP & Drawing Release Library.

For historical compatibility, the Legacy Ratio & Stage Reference remains available. It is no longer the primary product-discovery or download route.

For robot joint products, start with the Robot Joint Actuator Guide.

High-intent engineering comparisons:

  • How to Evaluate a Robot Joint Actuator Supplier
  • Planetary vs Cycloidal Reducer for Robot Joints
  • Integrated Robot Joint Actuator vs Motor + Gearhead
  • Robot Joint CAN, Encoder & Driver Selection

docs.title: Integrated Robot Joint Actuator vs Motor + Gearhead
docs.text:
A robotics team may choose either an integrated robot joint actuator or a separate motor + gearhead architecture. The better starting point depends on how much of the motor, controller, encoder, mechanical interface and joint packaging is already fixed.

SigGear supports both paths: published robot joint actuator platforms and 8–42 mm planetary gearheads that can be evaluated with an existing or selected motor.

docs.title: Quick Decision Guide
docs.text:
Project situation Practical starting point Motor, driver and control stack are already selected Gearhead-only or motor + gearhead integration review Team wants a compact joint package with motor, transmission and feedback reviewed together Integrated actuator reference Existing mechanism fixes the motor shaft and mounting pattern Gearhead / motor-interface review Joint envelope, torque and speed are known but electronics are open Compare integrated actuator and separate architecture Prototype needs fast mechanical packaging with public CAD Start from the closest released product platform Production design needs a special shaft, flange, cable or ratio Project-specific engineering review

This is a screening guide only. Final selection depends on the complete operating condition.

docs.title: Integrated Robot Joint Actuator
docs.text:
An integrated actuator can combine several functions in one joint package, depending on the selected model and configuration:

  • motor
  • reducer / gearbox
  • encoder or feedback device
  • output bearing structure
  • driver where applicable
  • cable / connector arrangement
  • joint-side mechanical interfaces

docs.title: Potential advantages
docs.text:
• fewer separate mechanical interfaces to define
  • compact packaging around one known joint envelope
  • easier early CAD integration when a released STEP model is available
  • motor, reducer and feedback can be reviewed as one system

docs.title: Items still requiring confirmation
docs.text:
• continuous and peak torque
  • peak duration
  • rated and maximum speed
  • driver and encoder version
  • communication interface
  • brake or power-off behavior
  • external loads
  • thermal condition
  • connector and cable configuration

Do not assume that every integrated actuator includes the same driver, encoder or communication protocol.

Browse SigGear Robot Joint Actuators

docs.title: Separate Motor + Gearhead Architecture
docs.text:
A separate architecture may be preferred when the robotics team already controls the motor, electronics or mechanical design.

Typical starting conditions include:

  • an existing BLDC, DC or other motor must be retained
  • the controller and encoder architecture are already fixed
  • only the reduction stage needs to change
  • the gearbox must fit an existing motor shaft and pilot
  • the output shaft or flange is application-specific
  • a smaller transmission is needed for a hand, gripper or auxiliary mechanism

SigGear publishes 8P–42P planetary gearhead platforms with public datasheets and CAD resources.

Browse 8–42 mm Planetary Gearheads Motor + Gearhead Integration

docs.title: If You Already Have a Motor
docs.text:
Send:

  • motor model or drawing
  • nominal voltage
  • rated / no-load speed
  • shaft diameter and usable length
  • mounting-hole pattern
  • locating pilot
  • required output speed
  • continuous and peak torque / load
  • maximum diameter and total assembly length

A preliminary ratio may be estimated from motor speed divided by target output speed, but the final configuration also needs stage availability, torque, efficiency, duty cycle and motor operating point.

docs.text:
When comparing an integrated actuator with a separate motor + gearhead, use the same boundary conditions:

docs.title: Miniature Planetary Gearbox Selector & Ratio Calculator (8–42 mm)
docs.text:
Quick Selector — Direct PDF, 2D and Full STEP Downloads

Use SigGear's online planetary gearbox selector to calculate a preliminary speed-reduction ratio and compare actual published 8P–42P planetary gearbox (gearhead) configurations by reduction ratio, stage count, rated output torque and gearbox body dimensions.

Enter your motor's loaded operating speed and desired output speed. If known, also specify the maximum diameter, gearbox body length, continuous output torque and peak load. Results link to model-specific Datasheets, Mechanical Interface information and a project brief for an engineering review.

This is an engineering preliminary selection tool, not a motor-sizing simulation. The application label, if supplied, never replaces the published torque, speed, geometry or duty-cycle checks. Actual motor compatibility and service life require engineering confirmation.

Open the Online Ratio & Stage Selector Compare 8–42 mm Planetary Gearboxes Browse Simplified STEP CAD Request Engineering Review

docs.title: Browse by Diameter Before Ratio Selection
docs.text:
If the mechanical envelope is already known, start from the exact gearbox diameter and then check stage-dependent length, ratio, torque and motor interface:

8 mm planetary gearbox · 10 mm · 12 mm · 14 mm · 16 mm · 20 mm · 22 mm · 24 mm · 28 mm · 32 mm · 36 mm · 42 mm

Diameter is only the first filter. Final selection still requires the exact ratio/stage, rated load, shaft loading, duty cycle and motor interface.

docs.title: 1. Decide What Needs to Be Supplied
docs.text:
Gearbox only: If you already have a motor, provide its model or drawing, operating shaft speed, shaft dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, locating pilot, available axial space and required output. Motor-to-gearbox interface and operating compatibility require review.

Motor + gearbox assembly: If the motor has not been selected, provide the power supply, desired output motion, load or torque, available diameter and total length, and operating cycle. SigGear can evaluate a motor with planetary gearbox as a complete matched assembly.

Open Motor + Planetary Gearbox Integration Guide

docs.title: 2. Estimate the Reduction Ratio From Loaded Speed
docs.text:
The preliminary reduction ratio is approximately motor speed at the operating point divided by target gearbox output speed. Do not automatically use the motor's no-load speed.

Compare this result with the published stage-specific ratio table of the selected gearbox. Different stages can change overall body length, torque rating and efficiency.

docs.title: SigGear Planetary Gearbox Selector
docs.text:
Use this tool for an initial comparison when you know the motor operating speed and target gearbox output speed.

What you enter: motor operating speed and target output speed; optionally maximum gearbox diameter, maximum gearbox body length, required continuous torque, peak torque and maximum ratio difference.

What you get: the closest published ratio, the smallest surviving frame and the shortest surviving gearbox among published configurations that satisfy the entered catalog filters. Requests outside the published limits can be submitted for engineering assessment.

It calculates:

preliminary target ratio = motor operating speed / target output speed

and compares that value with the currently published 1–4 stage ratios for SigGear 8P–42P.

Optional filters can remove configurations that exceed a maximum gearbox diameter, maximum gearbox body length, published rated allowable torque requirement, a maximum momentary torque screening threshold, or a user-defined maximum ratio difference. Exceeding a catalog limit does not rule out a customized solution; the results provide a custom engineering review path.

Motor operating speed (rpm) Target output speed (rpm) Maximum gearbox diameter (mm) — optional Maximum gearbox body length (mm) — optional Required continuous output torque — optional Torque unit N·m kgf·cm Required peak output torque — optional, preliminary screen Maximum ratio difference (%) — optional Find Published Configurations

Continuous input-speed range — engineering confirmed 15 October 2026: SigGear's 8P–42P planetary gearbox series supports Motor/configuration dependent; confirm selected operating point continuous input speed for preliminary standard-configuration selection, superseding the earlier published 8,000 rpm upper limit. Input speeds below 1,000 rpm or above 20,000 rpm are directed to custom feasibility assessment. The exact motor, ratio, duty cycle, thermal behavior, torque, and installation interface still require application-specific engineering review.

Torque and efficiency rules: published stage-specific rated allowable torque may be used for preliminary continuous-load screening; published maximum momentary torque may be used to rule out unsuitable peak-load candidates but does not establish an allowable peak duration or frequency. Exceeding either published torque threshold can be reviewed for customization. Published efficiency is a stage-level reference: ratio-specific differences are awaiting separate engineering verification. The tool does not infer motor suitability, safe peak duration, thermal behavior, service life or final design approval.

Important: this is a preliminary Design-In aid, not an automatic final selector. It does not add a safety factor, calculate motor shaft torque, predict service life, or prove that a customer's motor shaft / pilot / mounting pattern fits the gearbox.

The results now separate three different first-check questions:

  • Closest Ratio — the remaining published configuration with the smallest ratio difference.
  • Smallest Surviving Frame — the smallest diameter that still has at least one published configuration after your active filters.
  • Shortest Surviving Gearbox — the shortest published gearbox body among the remaining frame candidates.

These labels are not interchangeable and are not final recommendations. A smaller frame may have a less suitable ratio, and a shorter gearbox may have lower published rated torque. Confirm the selected model + stage + ratio + continuous / peak load + motor interface against the Datasheet and Mechanical Interface.

Existing Motor — Open Motor-Matching Workflow Open 8P–42P Datasheets & Mechanical Interfaces

docs.title: Worked Example: From Motor Speed to a Published Gearbox Ratio
docs.text:
For an illustrative mechanical design, suppose a motor operates at 6,000 rpm under the intended load and the mechanism needs approximately 140 rpm at the gearbox output.

  • Preliminary target ratio: 6,000 / 140 ≈ 42.86:1.
  • The published 12P, 3-stage, 42.9:1 configuration is one ratio to examine; its nominal outside diameter is 12 mm and its published gearbox body length is 16.85 mm.
  • Estimated gearbox output speed at that input speed: 6,000 / 42.9 ≈ 139.86 rpm. The published 3-stage rated allowable torque is 3.6 kgf·cm (approximately 0.353 N·m). Its stage-level reference efficiency is 73%.

This example is a calculation using catalog data, not a tested customer application or a final gearbox recommendation. It does not validate the motor's available torque, load margin, peak duration, shaft load, temperature or lifetime. See the 12P Datasheet and use the online selector for your own parameters.

docs.title: 3. Compare Continuous and Peak Torque Separately
docs.text:
• Normal running: Compare required continuous operating torque with the exact configuration's rated allowable torque, considering cycle and necessary margin.
  • Cutting, startup, impact or jam events: Consider magnitude, duration and frequency of peak loads. The published maximum momentary torque is not a continuous rating.
  • Motor matching: Output torque estimates depend on the motor shaft torque, selected ratio and the relevant gearbox efficiency. Use the efficiency published for the selected configuration, not a family maximum.

Never transfer a torque rating from one frame size or stage configuration to another without technical confirmation. If published torque, ratio, or envelope filters produce no catalog match, use Request Custom Engineering Review on the results page and attach the application / motor drawing. A successful preliminary match still needs review of actual operating conditions.

docs.title: 4. Check the Full Mechanical Interface
docs.text:
Measure the gearbox outer diameter, stage-dependent body length, output shaft, flange, mounting holes and motor-side shaft interface. Total motor-plus-gearbox assembly length is not the same as gearbox body length.

Output torque and shaft loads are different constraints. Review radial and axial forces, their application point and whether the mechanism needs an external bearing to support pulleys, pinions, cranks or other cantilevered loads.

Open Datasheets and Mechanical Interface References

docs.title: 5. Validate Backlash, Holding, Noise and Environment
docs.text:
A published gearbox backlash value is not a claim of zero backlash or final-system positioning accuracy. Do not assume a planetary gearbox is self-locking. If the design needs power-off holding, check brake and full-mechanism requirements.

Service life, sound level, ingress protection and corrosion resistance must be confirmed for the selected configuration and operating environment; do not infer unlisted ratings.

docs.title: 6. Use the Correct CAD
docs.text:
Public SigGear simplified 4-stage STEP references are available for 8P, 10P, 12P, 14P, 16P, 20P, 22P, 24P, 28P, 32P, 36P and 42P. They support preliminary external space and mounting checks while omitting internal planetary mechanism detail.

A 4-stage CAD reference is not interchangeable with a 1-, 2- or 3-stage configuration. For final Design-In, request the exact ratio/stage drawing and motor interface revision.

Download Public 4-Stage STEP Models

docs.title: Application-Specific Engineering Questions
docs.text:
An electric pruning-shear gearbox must be reviewed for blade geometry, cutting force variation, torque spikes and outdoor exposure. An electric curtain gearmotor needs track friction, pulley speed, acoustic, holding and safety reviews. A smart toilet or bidet mechanism adds low-noise, jam, humidity and cleaning-environment requirements. A dexterous hand or robot gripper requires finger-force or tendon-spool geometry, shaft-load and packaging review.

A smart lock or access-control mechanism adds bolt or latch preload, battery-current, jam and power-off requirements. Pump, valve and dosing mechanisms require pressure, seal friction, duty-cycle and feedback review. Camera focus, zoom and sensor-positioning mechanisms add backlash, vibration and repeatability constraints. Coffee, beverage and dispensing equipment adds dosing, jam, cleaning-boundary and acoustic requirements.

These are potential engineering uses, not published customer case studies.

docs.title: How do I calculate a planetary gearbox reduction ratio?
docs.text: Start with the actual motor speed under load divided by the required gearbox output speed, both in rpm. The resulting number is a target, not necessarily a published gearbox ratio. The selector compares that target against available 1–4 stage catalog ratios and reports the difference.

docs.title: Can I use the maximum momentary torque as a continuous rating?
docs.text: No. The selector checks continuous load against each stage's published rated allowable torque. Its separate peak-load filter uses published momentary limits only for preliminary exclusion; allowable peak duration, frequency and duty cycle need engineering review.

docs.title: Are the STEP CAD files exact for every selected ratio?
docs.text: No. Public simplified STEP references cover 4-stage frame geometry. A 1-, 2- or 3-stage configuration or a specific motor interface requires a configuration-matched drawing before production Design-In.

docs.title: What happens if no published configuration fits?
docs.text: The result offers Request Custom Engineering Review. Your speed and load requirements can be carried into an online project brief; a standard catalog no-match does not prove custom manufacturing is impossible.

docs.title: Planetary vs Cycloidal Reducer for Robot Joints
docs.text:
There is no universal rule that makes a planetary or cycloidal reducer the better choice for every robot joint. The correct architecture depends on the complete joint requirement: torque, speed, ratio, size, external loads, backlash target, thermal condition, backdrivability, motor selection, encoder / driver architecture and prototype constraints.

SigGear publishes both planetary robot joint actuators and cycloidal joint modules. The comparison below is an engineering screening guide, not a substitute for configuration-specific validation.

docs.title: Quick Comparison
docs.text:
Engineering question Planetary architecture Cycloidal architecture Transmission layout Coaxial multi-gear planetary stages Eccentric cycloidal reduction with output mechanism Ratio strategy Ratio depends on stage count and available gear combinations Ratio depends on the cycloidal mechanism and selected design Torque density Depends strongly on frame size, stages, materials and bearings Can be attractive where high reduction and compact joint packaging are required Backlash Must be checked for the exact gearhead or actuator configuration Must be checked for the exact cycloidal module and preload / assembly condition Efficiency Depends on ratio, stage count, speed, lubrication and load Depends on reduction mechanism, bearings, contact conditions, speed and load External loads Check output bearing and housing ratings Check output bearing and housing ratings Backdrivability Configuration-dependent Configuration-dependent Noise / vibration Depends on gear geometry, speed, load and assembly Depends on eccentric mechanism, bearings, speed, load and assembly Motor / driver integration Can be gearbox-only, motor + gearbox, or integrated actuator Can be reducer-centered or integrated joint module depending on the platform

Do not select a transmission architecture from one row alone.

docs.title: When a Planetary Solution Is Worth Evaluating
docs.text:
A planetary solution may be a practical starting point when the project needs:

  • a coaxial compact transmission
  • a wide choice of frame sizes and ratios
  • a gearbox-only solution for an existing motor
  • a motor + gearhead assembly
  • an integrated actuator based on a planetary transmission
  • a small-diameter transmission for hands, grippers, instruments or compact axes

SigGear publishes 8P through 42P planetary gearhead platforms and separate planetary robot-joint actuator references.

docs.title: When a Cycloidal Solution Is Worth Evaluating
docs.text:
A cycloidal solution may be worth evaluating when the project architecture favors:

  • high reduction in a compact joint arrangement
  • a dedicated joint-module structure
  • a different load path from a conventional multi-stage planetary gearbox
  • a robot-joint package where the reducer, bearings, motor and electronics are reviewed together

SigGear currently publishes CPM-78-39, CPM-80-25 and CPM-100-25 as cycloidal joint-module references. Their specifications belong to the listed configurations only.

docs.title: 1. Continuous and Peak Torque
docs.text: Define continuous torque, peak torque, peak duration and repetition. Do not compare one supplier's continuous rating with another supplier's short-duration peak value.

docs.title: 2. Output Speed
docs.text: Confirm rated and maximum output speed at the required torque. Maximum torque and maximum speed may not be available at the same operating point.

docs.title: 3. Installation Envelope
docs.text: Compare the complete installed diameter, thickness, motor length, output interface, connectors, driver space and cable bend radius.

docs.title: 4. External Loads
docs.text: A robot joint can apply radial, axial and overturning loads in addition to output torque. Check the complete bearing and housing arrangement rather than only the reducer torque rating.

docs.title: 5. Backlash, Accuracy and Repeatability
docs.text: These are different specifications. Use the exact published or confirmed value for the selected configuration and test method.

docs.title: 6. Backdrivability and Holding Behavior
docs.text: Backdrivability depends on ratio, friction, preload, motor cogging, brake state, lubrication and the complete mechanism. It should be tested in the actual or representative joint.

docs.title: 7. Thermal and Duty Cycle
docs.text: Define continuous motion, holding time, peak events, rest time, ambient temperature and cooling path. Joint packaging can strongly affect thermal behavior.

docs.title: 8. Encoder, Driver and Communication
docs.text: Confirm whether the project requires motor commutation feedback, output position feedback, integrated driver, external driver, CAN, RS485, EtherCAT or another interface. These functions are model- and configuration-specific.

docs.title: Quick Robot Joint Actuator Sizing Workflow
docs.text:
1. Define the joint position, payload, link geometry and complete motion cycle.
  2. Estimate gravity, acceleration and external-force torque.
  3. Separate continuous torque from peak torque and define peak duration.
  4. Check output speed, power, voltage and controller current limits at the same operating point.
  5. Confirm diameter, thickness, length, weight and external bearing loads.
  6. Compare planetary, cycloidal and integrated-actuator architectures.
  7. Confirm encoder, driver, communication, thermal and safety requirements.
  8. Validate the selected actuator in a representative prototype.

docs.title: Purpose of This Guide
docs.text:
A robot joint actuator should be selected from the complete axis requirement, not from one torque value or a product-family label. The joint position, payload, link geometry, acceleration, external forces, duty cycle, installation envelope, bearing loads, feedback architecture and controller limits all affect the final choice.

This guide provides a practical screening workflow for humanoid robots, quadruped robots, robotic arms, exoskeletons and other rotary-axis systems. Final model approval requires engineering review and prototype validation.

docs.title: Step 1: Define the Joint and Mechanism
docs.text:
Prepare a separate requirement sheet for each axis. A shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee or ankle normally has a different load case, motion profile and installation limit.

Record:

  • Joint or axis position
  • Payload and moving-link mass
  • Link lengths
  • Center-of-gravity locations
  • Joint angle range
  • External process forces
  • Mechanical stops and collision loads
  • Whether the axis is horizontal, vertical or gravity loaded
  • Customer-side bearings, belts, pulleys, gears or linkages

Do not apply one actuator specification to every axis of the robot.

docs.title: Step 2: Estimate Robot Joint Output Torque
Gravity Torque
docs.text:
For an initial one-axis estimate, gravity torque may be approximated by:

T_gravity = m × g × r × sin(theta)

where:

  • m is the supported mass
  • g is gravitational acceleration
  • r is the distance from the joint axis to the center of gravity
  • theta describes the mechanism orientation relative to gravity

The worst posture may not be the robot's normal operating posture, so review the full joint-angle range.

docs.title: Acceleration Torque
docs.text:
The torque required to accelerate the reflected inertia may be estimated by:

T_acceleration = J × alpha

where:

  • J is the total inertia reflected to the joint output
  • alpha is angular acceleration

Include the payload, links, tooling and any other moving components.

docs.title: External-Force Torque
docs.text:
An external force acting at a distance from the joint axis creates torque:

T_external = F × r

where F is the external force and r is the perpendicular lever arm.

docs.title: Preliminary Total
docs.text: A preliminary requirement should include gravity, acceleration, external forces, friction and mechanism losses. These equations are screening tools only. Flexible structures, impact, control behavior, load sharing and multi-axis dynamics may require a more complete model.

docs.title: Step 3: Separate Continuous and Peak Torque
docs.text: Continuous torque and peak torque are not interchangeable.

docs.title: Continuous Torque
docs.text: Continuous torque must cover sustained motion, repeated cycles and holding conditions without exceeding the approved thermal limits of the selected motor, gearbox and driver configuration.

docs.title: Peak Torque
docs.text:
Peak torque is used for short events such as acceleration, disturbance recovery, impact response or starting under load. Specify:

  • Required peak torque
  • Peak duration
  • Frequency of peak events
  • Time between peaks
  • Controller current limit
  • Battery or bus voltage
  • Cooling and ambient conditions

Never treat a published peak-torque value as a continuous rating.

docs.title: Step 4: Define Speed and the Complete Motion Cycle
docs.text:
Provide:

  • Rated output speed
  • Maximum output speed
  • Acceleration and deceleration
  • Travel angle
  • Cycle time
  • Holding time
  • Rest time
  • Direction-reversal frequency

Mechanical output power at an operating point is related to torque and angular speed:

P = T × omega

Torque and speed must be checked at the same operating point. A product's maximum torque and maximum speed may not be available simultaneously.

docs.title: Step 5: Establish the Installation Envelope
docs.text:
Define the maximum:

  • Outer diameter
  • Axial thickness
  • Total length
  • Weight
  • Cable and connector space
  • Driver-board space
  • Brake space
  • Mounting-flange envelope

Include the complete installed assembly, not only the reducer body. Bearings, output interfaces, covers, connectors and cable bend radius can consume significant space.

docs.title: Step 6: Review Radial, Axial and Overturning Loads
docs.text:
Output torque alone does not describe the structural load on a robot joint.

Provide:

  • Radial load
  • Axial load
  • Overturning moment
  • Load direction
  • Distance from the load to the output bearing
  • Impact or shock conditions
  • Customer-side bearing arrangement

The output bearing and housing must be evaluated together with the robot structure. An external bearing or additional support may be required when the joint has a large cantilevered load or overturning moment.

docs.title: Step 7: Define Positioning and Mechanical Behavior
docs.text:
Specify the completed-axis targets for:

  • Backlash
  • Positioning accuracy
  • Repeatability
  • Angular resolution
  • Stiffness or compliance
  • Backdrivability
  • Holding behavior
  • Direction-reversal response

Gearbox backlash is only one part of joint behavior. Encoder position, bearing clearance, housing stiffness, link compliance, assembly tolerances and controller tuning also affect the result.

docs.title: Step 8: Choose a Transmission and Product Architecture
docs.text: SigGear publishes both planetary joint actuators and cycloidal joint modules. Neither transmission type should be selected from a general rule alone.

docs.title: Planetary Joint Actuators
docs.text:
Planetary joint actuators may be evaluated when their published torque, speed, dimensions and configuration fit the application. SigGear's published planetary joint-actuator range includes SG-6010C, SG-6010D and SG-8021.

View planetary robot joint actuators

docs.title: Cycloidal Joint Modules
docs.text:
Cycloidal joint modules may be evaluated when the selected model's torque, speed, installation and configuration match the axis requirement. SigGear's published range includes CPM-100-25, CPM-80-25 and CPM-78-39.

View cycloidal joint modules

docs.title: Published Starting Points
docs.text:
Model Transmission Rated torque Peak torque Rated output speed Configuration note SG-6010C Planetary 6 Nm 18 Nm 310 rpm Driver and encoder functions depend on selected configuration SG-6010D Planetary 16 Nm 50 Nm 100 rpm Available with or without integrated driver SG-8021 Planetary 10 Nm 30 Nm 160 rpm Driver and encoder functions depend on selected configuration CPM-100-25 Cycloidal pinwheel 25 Nm 75 Nm 60 rpm Available with or without integrated driver CPM-80-25 Cycloidal pinwheel 10 Nm 50 Nm 120 rpm Available with or without integrated driver CPM-78-39 Cycloidal pinwheel 20 Nm 52 Nm 48 rpm Standard catalog configuration uses Hall sensors and has no integrated-driver claim

The table is a preliminary shortlist only. Dimensions, weight, external-load capacity, thermal behavior and control configuration must also be checked.

docs.title: Step 9: Define Encoder, Driver and Communication Requirements
docs.text:
Confirm whether the project requires:

  • Motor commutation feedback
  • Output absolute position
  • Incremental or absolute encoder
  • Position control
  • Velocity control
  • Torque or current control
  • CAN
  • RS485
  • EtherCAT or another project-specific interface
  • External controller or integrated driver
  • Required communication rate and protocol details

Driver, encoder, communication and closed-loop functions are model- and configuration-specific. Do not assume that every actuator includes the same electronics.

CPM-78-39 must be treated separately: its standard catalog configuration uses Hall sensors and does not support a general claim of an integrated driver or absolute encoder.

docs.title: Step 10: Review Voltage, Current and Power Architecture
docs.text:
Specify:

  • Nominal bus voltage
  • Minimum and maximum bus voltage
  • Continuous current limit
  • Peak current limit and duration
  • Battery or power-supply capability
  • Regenerative-energy handling
  • Emergency-stop behavior
  • Cable and connector current capacity

The controller current limit directly affects available torque. Electrical limits must be checked together with the motor, thermal design and duty cycle.

docs.title: Step 11: Evaluate Thermal Conditions and Duty Cycle
docs.text:
Provide:

  • Ambient temperature
  • Operating time
  • Holding time
  • Rest time
  • Cycle frequency
  • Enclosure and mounting material
  • Cooling method
  • Airflow or conduction path
  • Nearby heat sources

A joint mounted inside a sealed limb or compact housing may behave differently from the same actuator tested in open air. Prototype testing should reproduce the planned installation and motion cycle.

docs.title: Step 12: Define Brake, Safety and Power-Off Behavior
docs.text:
For gravity-loaded, wearable or safety-related axes, specify:

  • Whether the joint may move when power is removed
  • Required holding torque
  • Mechanical brake requirement
  • Emergency-stop behavior
  • Manual release requirement
  • Safe direction of motion
  • Collision or overload strategy

A brake must not be assumed to be included unless it is explicitly confirmed in the selected configuration and quotation.

docs.title: Step 13: Plan Prototype Validation
docs.text:
Prototype testing should include representative:

  • Payload and link geometry
  • Continuous motion cycles
  • Peak events
  • Temperature monitoring
  • Holding conditions
  • Direction reversals
  • Encoder behavior
  • Controller current limits
  • Communication behavior
  • External loads
  • Power-off and emergency-stop cases

Selection is complete only after the actuator is validated in the actual or representative mechanism.

docs.title: Requirement Checklist
docs.text:
Send the following information for engineering review:

Category Required information Application Robot type and joint position Mechanics Payload, link lengths, center of gravity and joint-angle range Torque Continuous torque, peak torque and peak duration Motion Rated speed, maximum speed, acceleration, deceleration and cycle time Electrical Voltage range, current limits and power source Packaging Maximum diameter, thickness, length and weight External loads Radial load, axial load and overturning moment Precision Backlash, accuracy, repeatability and resolution Control Encoder, driver, control mode and communication interface Environment Ambient temperature, cooling, contamination and duty cycle Safety Brake, holding and power-off behavior Commercial Prototype quantity and annual forecast

docs.title: Smaller Gearboxes for Hands and Auxiliary Mechanisms
docs.text:
If your engineering requirement is for a separate small gearbox rather than an integrated actuator, for example in an auxiliary adjustment axis, compact wrist mechanism or robotic gripper, review the SigGear 8–42 mm miniature and compact planetary gearbox range.

The Miniature Planetary Gearbox Selection Guide explains frame-size selection, motor matching, rated versus momentary torque, stage-dependent length and simplified 4-stage CAD. These small gearbox models must not be assumed suitable for a high-load humanoid joint without project-specific engineering validation.

docs.title: Robot Joint CAN, Encoder & Driver Selection Guide
docs.text:
A robot joint actuator should not be selected from torque and speed alone. The encoder, driver, control mode and communication interface must match the robot controller and the exact actuator configuration.

SigGear publishes joint products with different electronics arrangements. Do not assume CAN, RS485, EtherCAT, an integrated driver or an absolute encoder is standard across every model.

docs.title: Start With the Control Architecture
docs.text:
Before requesting a quotation, define which parts are already fixed:

  • robot main controller
  • motor driver
  • motor commutation feedback
  • output position feedback
  • communication bus
  • control mode
  • bus voltage
  • continuous and peak current limits

If these are still open, provide the robot architecture and the functions required from the joint.

docs.title: Encoder Questions
docs.text:
Clarify whether the project requires:

  • Hall sensors for commutation
  • motor-side encoder
  • output-side encoder
  • single-turn absolute position
  • multi-turn position
  • incremental feedback
  • redundant feedback
  • a specific resolution
  • a specific electrical interface

Encoder requirements affect mechanical packaging, wiring, calibration and driver compatibility.

docs.title: Driver Questions
docs.text:
Confirm whether the project requires:

  • an integrated driver
  • an external driver
  • position control
  • velocity control
  • torque / current control
  • FOC or another motor-control method
  • current and voltage limits
  • regenerative-energy handling
  • PC configuration / debugging tools

A published actuator may have several electronics variants. The quoted hardware and firmware configuration must be confirmed before prototype release.

docs.title: Communication Questions
docs.text:
Common project requirements can include:

  • CAN
  • RS485
  • EtherCAT
  • USB for configuration / debugging
  • another project-specific interface

The communication choice should be defined together with network topology, update rate, cable length, connector strategy, controller compatibility and required control modes.

docs.title: Why “Supports CAN” Is Not Enough
docs.text:
For a robot project, ask for the exact protocol and configuration rather than only the physical bus name.

Useful questions include:

  1. Is CAN physically available on this hardware version?
  2. Which messages and control modes are supported?
  3. Is the protocol fixed or project-configurable?
  4. Which encoder and driver version is used?
  5. What voltage and current limits apply?
  6. Is the communication documentation available for the quoted configuration?
  7. What PC tool or commissioning procedure is required?

docs.title: SigGear Product References
docs.text:
SigGear's published robot joint product pages identify model-specific electronics where available.

Planetary Robot Joint Actuators Cycloidal Joint Modules Robot Joint Datasheets & CAD

Where a product page labels an interface as optional, project-specific or subject to confirmation, treat it as not standard until confirmed in the quotation.

docs.title: Minimum Control Information to Send
docs.text:
For an engineering review, provide:

Category Information Main controller MCU, industrial controller, Jetson / PC or other controller Bus CAN, RS485, EtherCAT or other Control mode position, velocity, torque / current or mixed Feedback motor-side, output-side, absolute / incremental and required resolution Voltage nominal and maximum bus voltage Current continuous and peak current limits Joint behavior torque, speed, duty cycle and holding requirement Safety brake, power-off behavior and emergency-stop requirement Prototype quantity and planned test setup

docs.title: Mechanical and Electrical Selection Must Stay Connected
docs.text:
Changing the reducer ratio, motor, encoder, driver or supply voltage can change the available torque-speed operating point, thermal behavior, package length, wiring and control limits.

For that reason, final actuator selection should be reviewed as one configuration rather than as separate component specifications.

docs.title: How to Evaluate a Robot Joint Actuator Supplier
docs.text:
A robot joint actuator supplier should be evaluated on configuration-specific engineering evidence, not only on a torque headline or product photo.

For an early supplier comparison, ask whether the exact model under consideration has usable technical data, mechanical files, electronics information and a path from prototype validation to controlled production release.

docs.title: Supplier Evaluation Checklist
docs.text:
Area What to request or confirm Product identity Exact model and configuration being quoted Torque Continuous torque, peak torque, peak duration and test / operating condition Speed Rated and maximum output speed at the relevant operating point Size Complete OD, thickness / length, weight and connector envelope Mechanical interface Output flange / shaft, locating features, mounting pattern and datums CAD STEP model for packaging and design-in 2D drawing Interface dimensions, revision status and whether it is a reference or controlled drawing External loads Radial, axial and overturning load limits where applicable Encoder Exact encoder / feedback configuration and resolution if published Driver Integrated or external driver and the quoted hardware / firmware version Communication CAN, RS485, EtherCAT or another interface for the quoted configuration Thermal / duty cycle Continuous operation, hold time, peak events and cooling condition Prototype path Sample availability, validation plan and engineering review Production path Configuration freeze, controlled drawing and change-control process

A supplier should not be assumed to support a function simply because another model in the same family supports it.

docs.title: Public Engineering Files Matter
docs.text:
For design-in, the most useful public supplier evidence normally includes:

  • model-specific technical datasheet
  • 2D mechanical reference
  • STEP CAD
  • clear rated / peak torque definitions
  • model-specific driver / encoder / communication information
  • test data where available
  • engineering contact path for unresolved items

Public CAD is useful for packaging, but final production approval should still use the configuration-controlled interface and drawing revision.

docs.title: Questions for the Supplier Before Ordering a Prototype
docs.text:
1. Which exact model / variant is being quoted?
  2. What is the continuous torque, and under what duty / thermal condition?
  3. What is the peak torque, and how long can the peak be applied?
  4. Which STEP file and 2D drawing correspond to the quoted hardware?
  5. Is the drawing a reference copy or a revision-controlled production drawing?
  6. Which encoder is installed?
  7. Is the driver integrated or external?
  8. Which communication protocol is supported by this exact version?
  9. What current / voltage limits apply?
  10. What external bearing loads are permitted?
  11. What should be tested in the prototype before design freeze?
  12. What changes require a new drawing, firmware or configuration review?

docs.title: Supplier Comparison: Keep the Boundary Conditions Equal
docs.text:
Do not compare:

  • one supplier's peak torque with another supplier's continuous torque
  • reducer-only weight with another supplier's complete actuator weight
  • a driver-equipped CAD model with a no-driver mechanical version
  • a public reference drawing with a controlled manufacturing drawing
  • maximum speed at no load with rated speed under load

Use the same operating point and configuration boundary for every supplier.
